articles.title: Get Started with GPU-Accelerated DuckDB Analytics Using the Sirius Core Extension
articles.summary:
As datasets grow, analytical queries can take longer to run, slowing down data exploration, pipelines, and applications. For developers using DuckDB, reducing query times helps keep analytics responsive and can lower compute costs.
NVIDIA and DuckLabs collaborated to release Sirius as a DuckDB core extension, bringing GPU acceleration to DuckDB’s analytical query engine. With two SQL commands, you can install and load Sirius to accelerate supported analytical queries on NVIDIA GPUs without rewriting your SQL or changing database schemas.
Sirius, developed through a collaboration between the University of Wisconsin–Madison and NVIDIA, is an open-source, GPU-native SQL engine.
This post introduces the core extension, shows you how to run your first GPU query, and explains how Sirius integrates with DuckDB.
Accelerate DuckDB queries without rewriting SQL
Sirius accelerates supported queries as a whole. DuckDB handles SQL parsing and optimization, while Sirius executes the resulting query plans on the GPU. The core extension brings this capability into DuckDB’s standard workflow: install Sirius, load it, and run your queries.
With this release, you can:
- Install directly from DuckDB. Use INSTALL sirius; and LOAD sirius; to download and activate the extension.
- Retain familiar SQL. Execute supported analytical queries on NVIDIA GPUs without translating them into a separate GPU programming API.
- Use CPU fallback. Queries with unsupported features fall back to DuckDB’s CPU engine…

articles.title: Probing DNS at Cloudflare
articles.summary:
Probing DNS at Cloudflare
Imagine this: you’ve just pushed a release. All the unit tests passed and your dashboards are green. You sit back to relax but then suddenly your phone starts blowing up: prod is broken.
This is something the Cloudflare DNS team has experienced firsthand. In one rollout of the service that publishes DNS records to our edge, a scheduling bug let some record changes sit unpublished for hours. The service stayed up and was healthy, but new hostnames were slow to resolve and certificates couldn't be issued until the bug was squashed.
DNS failures are hard to catch because they are slow, spread across the network, and partial in where they cause impact. We needed to figure out a way to test DNS the way customers experience it: constantly, from every data center, and against production.
For us, the answer was to extend Flamingo, the end-to-end testing framework we were already using to run hundreds of millions of tests a day against Cloudflare's edge. This post covers how Flamingo's modular design lets us add DNS support, how we measure propagation, and how those measurements now decide whether a release goes ahead or gets rolled back.
A little background
At Cloudflare we’re obsessed with improving performance and safety for our customers. It’s crucial that our code is tested constantly, both at scale and against the real Cloudflare edge that our users operate in. That’s one reason why we created a tool called Flamingo: to measure the behavior of our produ…

It turns out: a lot. Anthropic closed its first day on the Nasdaq on Thursday with a market cap of nearly $1.3 trillion USD, the largest IPO in history.
Now, that solid debut isn’t a guarantee of continued momentum or overall faith in the AI trade, as anyone staring into a sea of red in their portfolios would have told you on Friday. Analysts have noted that it’s likely many traders dumped other tech stocks to give Anthropic a heavier weight in their portfolios. Meanwhile, lingering anxiety over inflation and massive capital expenditures on AI infrastructure contributed to a nasty end to the week as stock markets entered correction territory.
But as the first frontier company to test the waters, Anthropic appears to have found them decently warm.
Canada’s entrant in the frontier model race was watching closely, even though it doesn’t seem ready to jump in just yet. “A rising tide lifts all boats, and a very successful IPO is good for everyone,” Cohere co-founder Aidan Gomez wrote on X, congratulating Anthropic, followed by a small dig: “I hope Anthropic adjusts its strategy to support a healthy community of competitors and a diversity of different ideologies and opinions.”

articles.title: The catch in IBM’s offer to relocate its U.S.-based immigrant workers
articles.summary:
For some IBM employees, keeping their jobs could mean moving to another country — and taking a steep pay cut in the process.
Earlier this month, IBM said it would no longer support the U.S. immigration status of workers in its consulting division, offering them the option to take a role with the company in another country or exit, according to a Bloomberg report citing a company document.
“IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages,” an IBM spokesperson told Rest of World. “That participation has been declining for a number of years, and as skill availability and client need have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting.”
IBM Consulting employs more than 150,000 people globally. The company does not disclose the geographical split for its workforce, making it hard to ascertain the exact number of workers impacted by this decision. On November 19, the company’s career portal listed 1,278 open roles for the consulting division outside the U.S., including 1,125 in India, 23 in Singapore, and 18 in the U.K. In the U.S., it listed 89 roles.
For employees, relocation does not automatically ensure continued engagement, effective collaboration, or equal access to professional opportunities, Zakaria Laaraj, founder of consultancy Global New Ventures, told Rest of World. It may affect their access to decision-makers, established networks, and career opportunities…

Entre Orion, Arc, Dia, Atlas et tous les autres, ces dernières années n’ont pas été avares en nouvelles manières de surfer sur le web. Créer un moteur de rendu de zéro demande un tout autre travail, et c’est précisément ce qu’a annoncé la Ladybird Browser Initiative ce lundi 23 novembre.
En développement depuis longtemps, le navigateur Ladybird vient officiellement de sortir en version alpha avec son moteur maison. De quoi enfin concurrencer réellement Chrome et Firefox.
Sécurisez vos achats durant Black Friday avec la meilleure offre de l’année. Dénichez les bonnes affaires, Bitdefender s’occupe des arnaques.
Pourquoi c’est important d’avoir un nouveau moteur de rendu ?
Les plus vieilles et les plus vieux se souviendront sans doute d’une époque lointaine où le marché des navigateurs web était dominé par Internet Explorer 6 et où la plupart des sites web étaient « optimisés » pour le navigateur de Microsoft. Quiconque avait l’outrecuidance d’utiliser Firefox à l’époque était régulièrement confronté à des pages web qui ne fonctionnaient pas proprement, alors même que le logiciel respectait bien mieux les standards du web que son concurrent.

India recorded nearly 9.44 lakh average monthly searches for GTA VI-related terms, ranking sixth globally by search volume. However, it ranked 106th on a per-capita basis, according to a study by The Action Network.
India ranks sixth globally in total search volume for Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), recording approximately 943,900 average monthly searches for the game-related terms, according to a study by The Action Network.
However, when adjusted for population, India ranks 106th globally, with around 66 searches per 100,000 people. This highlights the difference between the scale of interest in a large market such as India and the intensity of interest among smaller populations.
The Netherlands topped the rankings with 2,045 average monthly searches per 100,000 people, followed by France (1,594), Finland (1,514), Switzerland (1,490) and Belgium (1,483). The Netherlands recorded 369,900 monthly searches despite having a population of approximately 18.1 million, compared with France's 1.09 million searches and population of 68.7 million.
Meanwhile, the United States recorded the highest overall search volume, with 3.06 million average monthly searches, followed by other major markets such as Brazil, Germany, France and the United Kingdom. However, the US ranked 22nd on a per-capita basis.

What it takes for Indian startups to win when building is no longer the hard part
At TechSparks 2026, Lukas Jablonskas of Hostinger and Amar Dixit of WOI India discussed how founders can turn ideas into sustainable businesses in the age of AI.
Building a product is no longer the biggest hurdle for many aspiring entrepreneurs. AI tools have made it easier to develop applications, test ideas, and bring solutions to market, but getting customers to use those products and building a sustainable business remain difficult. As more founders gain access to similar technology, understanding the market, finding the right distribution channels, and securing suitable funding become increasingly important.
At TechSparks 2026, Lukas Jablonskas, Head of WebPro at Hostinger, and Amar Dixit, CEO of WOI India, joined Madanmohan Rao, Research Director at YourStory, for a panel discussion titled ‘The New Startup Infrastructure: Expanding India’s Builder Economy’, exploring what it takes to build a globally relevant company from anywhere in India and how access to technology can be turned into sustainable entrepreneurship.
Understanding customers is still a competitive advantage

articles.title: CISA flags critical Cisco RCE flaw as actively exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
The US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) warned federal agencies that attackers are now exploiting a recently patched critical Cisco Expressway vulnerability in the wild.
Cisco Expressway Series devices are enterprise collaboration gateways (deployed as virtual machines or physical hardware appliances) that connect internal voice and video systems with outside networks and remote users via a secure connection.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466, this security flaw stems from the use of hard-coded credentials and a failure to fully validate client certificates, enabling unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute arbitrary operating system commands as root on affected Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E devices configured in a cluster.
"An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands," Cisco said in late October, when it released security patches to address the issue.
While Cisco says that its Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is not aware of active exploitation in the wild or publicly available proof-of-concept exploits targeting this vulnerability, CISA tagged it as actively exploited on Friday.
The cybersecurity agency also added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies to secure their systems within three days, as mandated by …

articles.title: Accelerating Direct Sparse Solvers for Computational Engineering with NVIDIA cuDSS 1.0
articles.summary:
Sparse linear systems are at the core of nearly every engineering and scientific simulation, from structural mechanics and computational fluid dynamics to circuit simulation and power grid analysis. As problem sizes and complexity grow, and accuracy needs tighten, developers need a direct solver that scales on GPUs without giving up the robustness that production simulations depend on.
The NVIDIA GPU-accelerated cuDSS library is designed to solve large sparse linear systems for engineering and scientific simulations. The general availability of cuDSS marked a major milestone, making it a production-ready library that developers and software vendors can confidently deploy in commercial applications.
This post walks you through how the cuDSS 1.0 release can help you with your applications. Specifically, it explains where industry-leading performance gains can be realized on real-world workloads, how the new pivoting and matching defaults improve accuracy on difficult symmetric indefinite systems, and how system-level optimization with intelligent use of GPU and CPU resources together enable solving problems at scale.
Enabling best performance for key computational engineering applications

articles.title: Jensen Huang reprend la tête de NVIDIA, onze jours après avoir démissionné
articles.summary:
NVIDIA avait mandaté un cabinet de recrutement pour trouver un successeur à Jensen Huang. Onze jours après sa démission, le groupe a choisi Jensen Huang.
Le conseil d’administration a officialisé son retour ce lundi 23 novembre. Le cofondateur reprend immédiatement ses fonctions de président et de directeur général et retrouve son siège au conseil. La décision a été prise à l’unanimité, après plusieurs réunions avec lui. Parmi les administrateurs qui ont voté son retour figure donc le président du conseil, Harvey C. Jones, qui l’écartait publiquement six jours plus tôt.

De la démission à la campagne pour son retour
Pour comprendre le revirement, il faut remonter au début du mois. articles.title: AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
articles.summary:
The clean energy revolution hinges on electrifying the entire global economy just as power-hungry data centers are surging. It’s a challenge delegates from all over the world had to grapple with during the United Nations climate conference, called COP31, that came to a chaotic and unsatisfying close in Antalya, Turkey, on Sunday.
AI data centers throw another wrench into chaotic UN climate talks
Global climate negotiations fell apart as delegates tried to tackle AI’s growing carbon footprint.
Each year, attendees try to make good on the commitment to stop climate change as part of the 2015 Paris climate accord. Preventing extreme weather from growing more terrifying, coastal communities from flooding, and droughts from wrecking food and water systems requires slashing greenhouse gas emissions. But in order to power homes or cars with solar and wind instead of oil and gas, they need to go electric.
“Every climate minister in the world is thinking about this”
To that end, one of the most anticipated outcomes of this year’s negotiations was a deal to raise electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035, compared to about 20 percent today. That becomes harder to do, however, when data centers are causing electricity demand to skyrocket. That made the rush of new AI data centers a climate issue alongside talks on how to transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy.

articles.title: Vale, Chris Dickman: Australian science grieves the loss of a giant of ecology and conservation
articles.summary:
Australia has lost one of its most distinguished ecologists and conservation champions, Emeritus Professor Chris Dickman.
Chris’s achievements and legacy are vast, much like his beloved Simpson Desert that he and his research team – known as “the ratcatchers” – have studied for well over 30 years. He and his team would camp out under the stars, carefully trapping and monitoring the desert’s animals and plants.
Without Chris, we wouldn’t know just how important even small but ferocious predators are in structuring ecological communities. One example is the brush-tailed mulgara, which preys on and regulates numbers of other predators, including the lesser hairy-footed dunnart.
Chris touched many in both his personal and professional roles. The authors of this article each knew Chris for many years.
Chris was honoured in a celebratory forum and festschrift, a collection of written tributes, in June that was attended by about 200 people and another 140 online. He died on November 17, 2026.
Science and service
Chris’s impressive career was marked by a dedication to the scientific field and service to the wider community.
He was an internationally renowned leader in wildlife conservation who studied everything from the small marsupial Antechinus to dunnarts, long-haired rats, mulgaras, quolls, sandy inland and spinifex hopping mice and the Tasmanian devil, to name but a few species.
His work shed light on the remarkable lives these animals lead as well as the challenges they face, …

articles.title: Uber now lets you book rides that record the drive by default
articles.summary:
Uber is piloting a new feature in the U.S. that offers rides in which drivers have enabled the company’s recording feature, Record My Ride.
The option, which uses the front camera of the Uber driver’s phone to record the entire drive, will show up as “Recorded Rides” in the app.
The ride-hailing company is starting the pilot in Baltimore, Raleigh, Indianapolis, and St. Louis and will expand to more locations later.
Uber said it is testing recorded rides specifically for rides booked at late night or those involving teens. Earlier this year, it introduced a live video streaming feature for rides booked for teenagers. In another test, the company had enabled audio recording for late-night trips in some cities.
The company is also testing a feature that will turn on recording when the app detects the ride going off-course, or when the vehicle might have had an accident.
The company said drivers can opt out of recording through the Settings panel. Similarly, riders can also decline permission to record their rides via an in-app notification.

In a March 2026 podcast interview, former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that he doesn’t believe in succession planning and that he could be CEO “until the last day of my life.” Seven months later, he resigned amid a scandal over his multiple alleged affairs, and his multi-billion-dollar company was left without a clear successor. 
Beyond the affair, this was Huang’s biggest mistake: believing that because he didn’t plan to exit the business, he didn’t need to plan for a successor or set the business up to run smoothly without him. Now, he’s been reinstated, perhaps further highlighting the company’s lack of a plan to move forward successfully without him at the helm.
“Think of your succession plan as a playbook for an absence.”
Every founder needs a succession plan, both for themselves and their key people, regardless of whether they plan to sell the business or not. Despite the importance, the CFIB reported in October that only six percent of Canadian small business owners have a formal written succession plan. We can’t predict the future; succession planning covers both planned absences, including parental leaves and sabbaticals, and unplanned absences due to illness, death, family caregiving requirements, or, like Huang, a public scandal.
If you’re a founder who falls into the 94 percent of business owners who don’t have a formal succession plan, here are the key steps to put in place.

Según advierte la Comisión Federal de Comercio de Estados Unidos (FTC), el engaño se apoya en dos factores: la urgencia y la necesidad de ayudar.
Quien llama puede decir que sufrió un accidente, que necesita pagar una fianza o que tuvo un problema con su auto. El estafador exige reserva. El objetivo es impedir que la víctima consulte con otros familiares antes de enviar el dinero.
Cómo un delincuente suplanta a un familiar
Los delincuentes pueden hacerse pasar por hijos, nietos u otros allegados a través de llamadas, mensajes y videollamadas. Para reforzar la identidad falsa, utilizan herramientas de inteligencia artificial capaces de imitar una voz a partir de audios disponibles en redes sociales, videos públicos o mensajes de voz.
La FTC alerta sobre la manipulación de imágenes. Una videollamada no garantiza que la persona al otro lado de la pantalla sea quien dice ser: los estafadores pueden crear o modificar videos para simular el rostro y los gestos de un familiar. La voz y la imagen ya no son pruebas suficientes de identidad.

articles.title: SAP NetWeaver, Cisco Expressway Flaws Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors have been exploiting SAP NetWeaver and Cisco Expressway vulnerabilities in the wild, the US cybersecurity agency CISA warned on Friday.
The NetWeaver flaw, tracked as CVE-2025-42884 (CVSS score of 6.5), is a medium-severity issue that could allow unauthenticated attackers to leak or modify server information.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to “inject JNDI environment properties or pass a URL used during JNDI lookup operations, enabling access to an unintended JNDI provider,” reads a NIST advisory.
SAP patched the bug with its November 2025 security updates. There appear to have been no reports of the security hole being exploited in the wild before CISA’s Friday alert.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS score of 9.8), the Expressway defect is a critical hardcoded credentials weakness that could allow attackers to execute system commands with root privileges.
The use of persistent cookies, combined with insufficient validation of client certificates in certain conditions, could allow attackers who possess the cookies to connect to the database service and invoke specific RPC commands.
It impacts Expressway Core (Expressway-C) and Expressway Edge (Expressway-E) devices running vulnerable software versions and configured in a cluster, and was patched on October 21 in Expressway Series release X15.5.20.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

They say that to understand where an industry is heading, you have to follow the money. And two acquisitions announced this past week suggest that established infrastructure vendors see a big opportunity in helping enterprises take greater control of the AI systems they deploy — and ensuring those systems are secure, reliable and trustworthy.
In early November, Applied Compute, a startup specializing in post-training and inference for open-weight AI models, announced it had raised $350 million at a $3.25 billion valuation, less than 18 months after its founding. The following day, search and observability giant Elastic announced plans to acquire HoneyHive, a four-year-old startup specializing in AI agent observability and evaluation.

Visa annonce étendre son programme Agentic Ready aux commerçants et aux prestataires de paiement européens. Plus de 85 acteurs, dont Adyen, Stripe et Worldline, vont tester les achats réalisés par des agents IA, avant un prochain déploiement.
Le géant Visa a annoncé, ce lundi 23 novembre, l'extension de son programme Agentic Ready aux commerçants, aux prestataires de services de paiement et aux acquéreurs européens. Avec l'identification des agents, la sécurisation des transactions mais aussi les premiers retours de terrain, les participants disposent désormais d'un cadre commun pour passer aux tests réels.
Visa veut que les commerçants européens puissent vendre à des agents IA

articles.title: „Wie einen Donut auf dem Mond fotografieren“: So schwierig war das erste Bild eines Schwarzen Lochs
articles.summary:
„Wie einen Donut auf dem Mond fotografieren“: So schwierig war das erste Bild eines Schwarzen Lochs
Schwarze Löcher faszinieren die Wissenschaft schon lange. Dabei handelt es sich um Bereiche im Weltall mit so starker Gravitation, dass nichts mehr aus ihnen entkommen kann – nicht einmal Licht. Schwarze Löcher entstehen, wenn sehr viel Masse auf kleinstem Raum konzentriert ist und die Raumzeit dadurch stark gekrümmt wird.
Nach Albert Einsteins allgemeiner Relativitätstheorie wird die Raumzeit von Masse gekrümmt. Bei einem Schwarzen Loch ist diese Krümmung so stark, dass selbst Lichtstrahlen nicht mehr nach außen gelangen können.
Die Aufnahme mit der Bezeichnung M87* erlangte weltweite Bekanntheit
Im April 2019 wurde das erste von der Menschheit aufgenommene Bild eines supermassereichen Schwarzen Lochs der Öffentlichkeit präsentiert. Es entstand mithilfe des Event Horizon Telescope (EHT), einem weltweiten Verbund von Radioteleskopen. Das Bild zeigt das supermassereiche Schwarze Loch im Zentrum der Galaxie Messier 87 (M87), die 55 Millionen Lichtjahre von uns entfernt ist. Die Aufnahme, die weltweite Bekanntheit erlangte, bekam die Bezeichnung M87*.
Siebeneinhalb Jahre später hat ein unabhängiges Forschungsteam dieses Bild jetzt verifiziert. Dies bestätigt Einsteins allgemeine Relativitätstheorie, die bereits die Existenz Schwarzer Löcher sowie das Aussehen ihrer unmittelbaren Umgebung vorhersagte. Die Forschungsergebnisse des Teams sind in der Fachzeitschrift Nature veröffentli…

articles.title: Verifying UCIe.mem: Flexible Verification For Compute And Memory Chiplets
articles.summary:
Validate UCIe.mem implementations across development stages while reusing a common verification environment.
By Ujjwal Negi and Prashant Dixit
As chiplet-based designs become increasingly common, connecting compute and memory dies efficiently is an important part of building scalable systems. The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) standard provides a common die-to-die interconnect, while UCIe.mem defines a standardized protocol for memory transactions between compute and memory chiplets.
Modern systems can combine compute chiplets with different memory technologies, including HBM, DDR, and LPDDR. Traditionally, integrating these components can involve technology-specific interfaces and custom mechanisms. UCIe.mem addresses the growing need for scalable and flexible memory architectures in modern computing systems by providing a common, memory-technology-agnostic way to communicate memory requests and responses across chiplets.
This standardization provides a foundation for more modular and scalable chiplet-based architectures. It allows compute and memory chiplets to be developed independently and integrated across implementations from different vendors, reducing reliance on custom, technology-specific interfaces. By decoupling memory communication from the underlying memory technology, UCIe.mem gives system designers greater flexibility to combine, reuse, and scale compute and memory resources to meet different application requirements.

articles.title: Nvidia reverses course and brings Jensen Huang back as CEO
articles.summary:
In a stunning reversal, Nvidia’s board said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as the company’s CEO and president, less than two weeks after he resigned following his admission of at least two extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman whom the U.S. government suspects to be a Chinese spy.
The decision marks an extraordinary comeback for one of the tech industry’s most influential executives, whose abrupt departure raised questions about national security and the future of the world’s most valuable chipmaker. Notably, the U.S. government itself played a role in his return: Nvidia’s board said it consulted senior government officials before determining that Huang posed no national security risk.
Nvidia shares, which had already shot up in premarket trading, opened 30% higher. Nvidia shares were priced at $159.95 a share, up 27%, at 9:51 a.m. ET.
In the days since Huang resigned, President Donald Trump has repeatedly expressed his support for the ousted executive, who is now back at the helm of the AI chip giant. Trump said in a post on Truth Social that the board “made the correct and proper decision to return” Huang to the position, noting that the U.S. government has no reason to believe that Nvidia poses any risk to national security.
Trump also said the U.S. attorney general confirmed that the U.S. government doesn’t have any evidence that Huang engaged in any illegal activity.

articles.title: BadBox 3.0 Ad Fraud Operation Generating 40 Billion Daily Bid Requests Disrupted
articles.summary:
Bot and fraud protection firm Human Security says it has disrupted the largest ad fraud botnet by bid volume.
Dubbed BadBox 3.0, it is the third iteration of a large operation targeting low-cost Android devices. The first BadBox botnet ensnared more than 190,000 devices, while BadBox 2.0 was initially found on over 1 million devices, but eventually ensnared more than 10 million.
“At its height, BadBox 3.0 accounted for roughly 40 billion bid requests a day and more than 4% of all CTV traffic observed by the Human Defense Platform,” Human Security says, noting the bid request volume was three times the volume recorded for the VastFlux ad fraud scheme.
Portions of BadBox 3.0, the cybersecurity firm says, were operated via command-and-control (C&C) domains that were disrupted when Google took down XCPE, a botnet of over 1.3 million Android set-top boxes.
The botnet consists of low-cost, uncertified Android Open Source Project devices infected with backdoors delivering fraud modules designed to render hidden video ads and to enroll the devices into residential proxy networks.
Human Security says its Satori Threat Intelligence and Research Team has uncovered an actively maintained catalog of fraud modules hosted on public repositories, as well as links to Chinese electronics manufacturer TXCZ. Some of the modules were previously seen in BadBox and BadBox 2.0.

articles.title: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
articles.summary:
In this podcast, Michael Stiefel spoke to Zhou Yu about using dynamic simulations to evaluate AI agents. One particular focus was conversational agents where actions depend on prior responses, and the non-deterministic nation of LLMs means you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks.You need to test them using dynamic simulations that incorporate different personas, goals, and corner cases. You can simulate how conversations shift based on moods, preferences, accents, or environmental conditions such as factory background noise. Rather than relying on simply binary pass or fail, the rule based task verifiers can measure whether the task was completed as well as threshold metrics for cost, efficiency, safety, and compliance.
Simulations can be used during the entire software lifecycle. Product managers can use them for prototyping and design. Engineers can use them for testing in CI/CD pipelines. They can also be used to test production for model drift or failure of third party tools. They can also be used to test compliance with the laws in different regions. Simulations can also be used with synthetic data to fine-tune models.
Key Takeaways
- To evaluate AI agents you cannot rely on static, reference-based benchmarks because the systems are not deterministic, and often the results depend on prior responses. Testing requires using dynamic simulations that can incorporate personas, goals, and corner cases.

articles.title: Telecom giant Bell says “agentic threat actor” accessed customer information
articles.summary:
Canadian telecommunications giant Bell and its subsidiaries have been breached by an “agentic threat actor.”
The news: On Nov. 17, an unknown party gained unauthorized access to an internal Bell system that included customers’ personal information, the company told customers in an email on Monday morning. The breach was carried out by an “agentic threat actor” and affected Bell and subsidiaries, including Bell Aliant, Bell MTS, Virgin Plus, and Lucky Mobile, the company told BetaKit in an email.
Bell told customers that impacted personal information may have included names, mailing addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, and account details such as account numbers, product information, business names, as well as the date and amount of their last payments. Bell added that highly sensitive personal information, such as credit card numbers or bank account information, was not affected.
From the source: “Upon discovering the incident, Bell immediately removed the threat actor and initiated emergency protocols,” Bell told customers in the email. “We continue to monitor all systems closely. We take our obligation to safeguard your information very seriously and we have engaged the RCMP’s cybercrime unit to investigate.”
The context: High-profile cybersecurity incidents have been common this year, beginning with an OpenAI model hacking Hugging Face over the summer. This past month, in particular, has seen numerous cybersecurity failures, including at Canadian accounting firm KPMG…

The company late last month said its outcome-based pricing model has helped it double its run-rate revenue to $400 million within five months.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: Newer AI models are swearing more, and it usually means they're failing
articles.summary:
WTF?! Large language models trained after July 2026 swear more often than earlier systems, according to a report by AI analyst firm Vals. The profanity rarely reaches users because it appears almost entirely in the models' chain of thought, the step-by-step reasoning a system writes out before giving its final answer. When the swearing does appear, it tends to signal trouble, since runs that contained it succeeded far less often than runs that did not.
Connor Frank, who wrote the Vals report, summed up the pattern. "Models swear when stuck, and mostly to themselves," he told The Economist.
Vals did not try to catalog every form of crude language. It tracked the word "fuck" and its variants, along with a small set of milder outbursts. Even with that limited word list, the gap between models was wide. Of the 102 models assessed, 88 never swore, and they avoided even the abbreviation "WTF." At the other end, MiMo V2.6 Pro, a frontier model released by Chinese tech giant Xiaomi in September, cursed in more than 8% of its transcripts.
The rise in swearing runs counter to how these systems are usually built. Profanity used under stress is common in the human-written text that models learn from during pretraining. Developers then apply reinforcement learning, a later training stage in which outputs are ranked using human feedback and the model is pushed toward responses people prefer. articles.title: NVIDIA's SSD Writing Bug Needs Another Hotfix as Issue Returns
articles.summary:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
NVIDIA's SSD Writing Bug Needs Another Hotfix as Issue Returns
Last week, NVIDIA released the GeForce Hotfix 621.35 driver to address the issue of excessive SSD writing that many consumers reported on their systems. However, the problem might not be completely resolved, and another update could be necessary, as more reports of SSD writing are resurfacing in online communities. According to a Reddit thread, a user reported that the latest hotfix has reduced the peak writing rate seen with the previous GeForce Game Ready 621.24 driver, and that the writing doesn't immediately start after a reboot. However, after a longer uptime or a sleep/wake transition, the writing continues at a rate of 1.26 MB/s, compared to the previous rate of up to 9.1 MB/s. Notably, this issue was recorded on the GeForce RTX 4090 SKU, and the user states that the only way to stop the NVDisplay.Container.exe writing loop is by rolling back to the 621.01 driver version or disabling the _nvtopps container plugin by setting DisableLoad to 1.
NVIDIA's staff on the GeForce Forums confirms that the bug doesn't affect any of the GeForce RTX 50 series "Blackwell" graphics cards. We are monitoring to see if the issue returns for the latest GeForce series as well. In the meantime, it appears that only the GeForce RTX 40 "Ada Lovelace" series is affected, and another hotfix might be needed to resolve the SSD writing bug for good.

articles.title: AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos
articles.summary:
Threat actors breached at least three AI inference providers and stole customer prompts, but none detected the intrusions until they were notified, according to cybersecurity firm Dragos.
AI inference providers host AI models and sell access to them through APIs. The hacks were detected after a team led by Dragos chief research officer HD Moore sent out roughly two million prompts to widely used AI services between July and November.
These prompts contained a unique, trackable bait such as URLs, hostnames, and credentials, including AWS keys. The security firm then set up a monitoring system to see whether anyone used the bait information in the wild, which meant the prompt had been compromised.
Dragos soon found evidence indicating that someone had stolen information from one of the tested AI inference providers. 
“Although our prompts were bait, they were processed along with real customer requests, and those were almost certainly copied too,” Moore noted.
The biggest breach involved roughly 200 AWS test keys sent to a provider, which were stolen in late October.
“Some of the stolen keys came from requests that the provider rejected before a model ever ran – this tells us that the attacker was copying requests at the provider’s front door, and not somewhere deeper in the inference stack,” Moore said.
Dragos saw the attackers checking which stolen keys worked, then trying to use them to obtain valuable data from the associated accounts.
The attackers have not been identified…

articles.title: OPINION: AI will favour the companies built for AI, not adapted to it
articles.summary:
For decades, business leaders have been warned that the impending arrival of a new technology will completely reorder the corporate world. But for the best part of the last thirty years, it did not.
The web, mobile phones, cloud computing and social media, for example, were all predicted as disruptors that would sweep the incumbents aside.
With AI, however, the warning deserves more consideration. The reason is less to do with the technology itself, but rather who is best placed to use it, and that is increasingly becoming startups, rather than established companies.
The web didn’t break incumbents
The common story of the web is that of upstarts bringing down giants, and the rankings seem to agree.
The world’s most valuable company in 1995 was a Japanese telephone operator. In the same year, Microsoft barely made number twenty on the list and Nvidia was just a startup. Today Microsoft, Nvidia, Apple, Amazon and Alphabet lead the rankings, and just six of the largest companies in 1995 remain in the top thirty.
Though on closer examination, the incumbents were not the disasters the ranking implies.
Companies such as Exxon, Coca-Cola and Toyota, more than tripled their combined revenue between 1994 and 2024, meanwhile Microsoft grew more than fiftyfold. The web gave them access to better logistics, cheaper computing and wider reach. Oil companies could use better software without becoming software companies. Carmakers could run a more efficient supply chain. And a wealthier worl…

articles.title: Durante las excavaciones arqueológicas en la Duna de Pilat, estos científicos descubrieron restos que datan de la Edad del Hierro
articles.summary:
Un grupo de arqueólogos ha encontrado restos de la Edad del Hierro en la duna de Pilat, situada en la región francesa de Gironda. El descubrimiento tuvo lugar durante unas excavaciones realizadas entre el 21 de septiembre y el 9 de octubre de 2026, en las que participaron investigadores y voluntarios. Entre los objetos encontrados hay piezas de cerámica, algunas de ellas especialmente bien conservadas.
De hecho, el arqueólogo Philippe Jacques explicó que habían recuperado una vasija prácticamente completa, desde la base hasta el cuello, algo que no suele ser habitual en este tipo de excavaciones. Sin embargo, lo más interesante llegó cuando encontraron varios objetos relacionados con la pesca, entre ellos un flotador, una piedra utilizada como peso para las redes y lo que podrían ser fragmentos de una herramienta para repararlas.
Un descubrimiento que aporta nuevas pistas sobre la zona
¿Y por qué es importante este hallazgo? Porque, como explica Jacques en unas declaraciones difundidas por el organismo que gestiona la duna de Pilat, hasta ahora no habían encontrado pruebas de actividades pesqueras durante la Edad del Hierro en esa parte de la costa francesa. articles.title: AWS launches 5 new open decision models for AI agents
articles.summary:
AWS launches 5 new open decision models for AI agents
AWS on Monday launched Strands Decider v2, a family of five open decision models.
The release comes only seven weeks after Strands Labs, the experimental arm of AWS’s open source Strands Agents SDK, launched the first Strands Decider model. That was a 2-billion-parameter model built on Alibaba’s Qwen3.5.
The new version is based on Google’s Gemma 4 and comes in a range of sizes from the outset, starting at 2 billion parameters, all the way up to a 31-billion-parameter dense model (with a 4B model and a 26B-A4B mixture-of-experts model in the middle), all of which are available under the Apache 2.0 license.
Like similar decision models, the idea behind Strands Decider is that it doesn’t generate text. Instead, it takes a state, like a support ticket or an agent trace, along with a question and a fixed set of possible answers, and then returns a probability for each answer.
AWS VP and Distinguished Engineer Marc Brooker, who started the project, tells The New Stack, “We chose better training data or larger training sets, the usual kind of ML model generation journey, and came out with a set of models with significantly better accuracy and significantly better calibration, which are the things that really matter to customers in this space.”
Benchmarks

articles.title: Los jóvenes están cada vez más ansiosos y este factor psicológico es una de las principales causas
articles.summary:
Que los jóvenes tienen más problemas de ansiedad que las personas de más edad es algo que tenemos más que comprobado. Si los millennials ya veníamos pisando fuerte en ese sentido, los más jóvenes (porque los millennials también somos jóvenes, ¿vale?) lo tienen aún más crudo. En España los trastornos de ansiedad son el problema de salud mental más registrado en la adolescencia, con 34,6 casos por cada 1.000 habitantes. Pero no es solo una cuestión española.
En Estados Unidos, por ejemplo, también se está dando cada vez más esta tendencia. Por eso es tan importante el estudio realizado recientemente por un equipo de científicos de la Universidad de Columbia. Y es que, tras analizar cómo ha evolucionado un importante factor psicológico a lo largo de los años, han comprobado que puede ser el quid de la cuestión. Se trata de la intolerancia a la incertidumbre y conocerla es muy importante.
El término. La intolerancia a la incertidumbre (IU por sus siglas en inglés) hace referencia a la tendencia a angustiarse, preocuparse o evitar situaciones cuando no se sabe qué va a pasar. Aunque no se sabe con seguridad quién lo acuñó, se le atribuye ampliamente a un grupo de investigadores canadienses de la Universidad Laval, por el artículo “Why do people worry?”, publicado en 1994 en la revista Personality and Individual Differences. Textualmente, ellos lo describieron como una serie de “reacciones cognitivas, emocionales y conductuales ante la incertidumbre en situaciones cotidianas”.

articles.title: Claude Code Adds Experimental Code Mode to Orchestrate Tool Calls with JavaScript
articles.summary:
Anthropic has added Code Mode to Claude Code, an experimental feature in which the model writes JavaScript to drive its tools instead of requesting each Bash, Read, or Edit call separately. Code Mode is off by default, requires Claude Code v2.1.323 or later, and is enabled with the CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE=1 environment variable. Anthropic warns it may change or be removed in any release.
In a normal session, Claude asks for one tool call, reads the full result, and decides the next step. In Code Mode, one script can run commands in parallel, pass one result into the next call, and return only the output the model needs. The documentation's example finds a file with rg, raises a retry limit, runs the tests, and returns just the path and test output. The conversation still shows each tool call and diff, while the generated code sits in the transcript viewer. Anthropic recommends it for edits repeated across many files, searches that need filtering, and independent commands. Code that Claude waits on stops after ten minutes; sessions started in auto or bypassPermissions mode can push it to the background for up to two hours while the conversation continues.
The permission model is the part architects should read first. Each call inside a script still goes through deny and ask rules and PreToolUse hooks, but in auto mode the classifier reviews the script before it runs, not each call, and cannot see values computed at run time. articles.title: Taking a personal loan with variable income? Here's how to plan your EMI smartly
articles.summary:
Taking a personal loan with variable income? Here's how to plan your EMI smartly
From assessing affordability to choosing the right tenure, freelancers and self-employed borrowers can use an EMI calculator to navigate loan repayments with greater confidence.
For freelancers and self-employed professionals, monthly income can fluctuate significantly. One month may bring several projects, while the next may be quieter. This makes fixed loan repayments harder to plan. An EMI calculator can help estimate monthly instalments, but borrowers with variable income should also build a repayment strategy that accounts for slower months.
Why variable income requires careful EMI planning
Unlike salaried employees, freelancers may not receive the same amount every month. Business owners can also experience seasonal changes in revenue, delayed client payments, or unexpected expenses.
Before taking a Rs 1 lakh loan, consider your average monthly income rather than basing affordability on your strongest earning month. Reviewing income over several months can provide a more realistic picture of what you can comfortably repay.
How an EMI calculator helps
An EMI calculator uses the loan amount, interest rate, and repayment tenure to estimate the monthly instalment. This allows borrowers to test different combinations before committing to a loan.

articles.summary:
Google dá prazo para apps de Android ganharem versões dobráveis
Apps que não se adequarem às regras de telas dobráveis perderão o direito de publicar novas versões e terão menos alcance na Google Play Store.
O Google determinou que, a partir de abril de 2027, desenvolvedores atendam ao Nível 3 (Tier 3) das diretrizes de qualidade adaptável do Android para dispositivos dobráveis. Na prática, isso significa que um app não poderá funcionar de modo improvisado quando expandido para uma tela maior.
Talvez você já tenha passado pela experiência de usar um app em celular convencional e, ao abri-lo em um smartphone dobrável ou até em um tablet, notar que ele ficou com elementos desalinhados ou com grandes áreas não aproveitadas, por exemplo. É justamente esse tipo de situação que o Google quer evitar com as novas diretrizes.
Para tanto, há uma série de exigências a serem seguidas. Uma delas determina que a interface do aplicativo continue funcional quando houver mudança de orientação ou de dimensões, o que ocorre quando o usuário abre ou fecha a tela dobrável.
Outra exigência determina que o app ocupe de modo adequado o espaço oferecido por uma tela expandida, não podendo exibir seu conteúdo como se estivesse em um celular convencional (com visor estreito). Vai além: o aplicativo também deve suportar modos de múltiplas janelas.

Z.ai ran the same 28 layers twice — and claims its 750B model can rival a 3-trillion-parameter one
Z.ai released GLM-5.4 on Monday, introducing a Loop Transformer architecture that executes the same layers multiple times to increase computational depth without adding parameters.
The company claims its 750-billion-parameter model can match the reasoning performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters…
The company claims its 750-billion-parameter model can match the reasoning performance of models with 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameters, although it has not published full-scale benchmarks to support that comparison.
Built by continuing to train GLM-5, the model runs a shared block of 28 layers twice during inference. Z.ai developed the architecture for demanding coding and agentic workloads.
Depth without more parameters
Z.ai chose to modify a pretrained model after earlier experiments showed that looped Transformers trained from scratch performed worse than conventional models given the same pretraining compute.
Repeating layers at this scale created problems with activation stability and attention caching. Z.ai introduced per-token gates to regulate updates to the residual stream and prevent activation norms from growing across iterations.
GLM-5.4 shares the first iteration’s KV cache and maintains a separate sliding window for the second pass, avoiding the memory cost of duplicating the entire attention history at context lengths of up to one million tokens. …

articles.title: phpAfterShell Vulnerability Revives PHP2Shell’s Attack Path
articles.summary:
PHP last week patched a critical-severity vulnerability residing in the same dangerous state as the PHP2Shell flaws, cybersecurity firm Depthfirst says.
Dubbed phpAfterShell, the security flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-126714 (CVSS score of 9.2), and was resolved on November 19 alongside six other critical issues.
According to Depthfirst, the bug could allow an attacker who can control data written to a session file and interrupt the session write operation to trigger an object deserialization and achieve remote code execution (RCE).
It exists because PHP overwrites the session file from the start without emptying it first. articles.title: A Link Is Not Architecture: Why Multi-Die Systems Need More Than Die-to-Die Connectivity
articles.summary:
Maintaining consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations.
The system-on-chip (SoC) transformed semiconductor design by bringing the major functions of an electronic system onto one die, an integration that shaped chip architecture for years. Multi-die design is now changing the model again, distributing system functionality across multiple dies within a single package.
While this approach gives engineers greater flexibility to align semiconductor design with system requirements, bringing these designs to life takes more than a die-to-die link to transport transactions across the package. It requires a system architecture that manages how data moves between dies.
In AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems, multi-die architectures enable teams to scale compute and select an appropriate process technology for each part of the design. These partitioning choices determine which transactions remain within a die and which must cross die boundaries. Treating each boundary independently increases integration and verification effort, complicates performance management, and reduces the practical value of chiplet reuse.
Still, managing communication across these die boundaries requires a clear separation between the physical interface that transports transactions and the system architecture that manages them. articles.title: Dutch privacy authority urges consumers not to buy 'pervert glasses'
articles.summary:
The Dutch Data Protection Authority is urging consumers not to buy AI-enabled camera glasses, warning that they compromise the privacy of nearby bystanders and risk the safety of their users.
The authority, whose recent statement falls just short of an outright ban, said that use of the internet-enabled and always-on glasses to record people in public is “almost always prohibited.”
Critics have dubbed these smart wearables as “pervert glasses” for their propensity to be used to video people without their permission, particularly to harass women. While some glasses have warning lights when users are recording, privacy advocates have argued that these alerts are not clear enough. Some people have even made phone apps capable of detecting nearby smart glasses wearers.
The Dutch data protection authority warned that the glasses also produce wrong results and unsafe results. In one test carried out by the Dutch authority, a pair of unnamed glasses “gave dating advice to an adult who indicated that they are interested in a minor.” The glasses also incorrectly read a medicine label and claimed to have called an ambulance when it had not.
The Dutch government’s advice follows a similar move by the Norwegian government, which in September said it was considering a ban on camera-enabled devices.

OpenJDK
Oracle has released versions 27.0.1.0.3, 25.0.5.0.3, 21.0.13.0.3, 17.0.21.0.3, 11.0.33.0.3 and 8u511b3 of the JDK as part of their quarterly Critical Security Patch Update Advisory for November 2026. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes for version 27.0.1.0.3, version 25.0.5.0.3, version 21.0.13.0.3, version 17.0.21.0.3, version 11.0.33.0.3 and version 8u511 b33.
JEP 547, Lazy Constants (Fourth Preview), has been elevated from Proposed to Target to Targeted for JDK 28. This JEP proposes a fourth preview, with no changes, after three rounds of preview delivered in the upcoming release of JDK 27 and JDK 26 through JDK 25. articles.title: JEP 545 Moves ZGC Memory Preparation off the Startup Path in JDK 28
articles.summary:
JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been integrated into JDK 28, moving the work of acquiring and preparing heap memory off the startup path and onto dedicated concurrent worker threads. On Linux 6.1 and later it also upgrades 4 KB pages to 2 MB pages while the application runs. The 2 MB initial heap behind the JEP's headline numbers comes from elsewhere: adaptive heap sizing, in the companion JEP 546, which still defaults to off.
Deploying ZGC has until now meant choosing which half of a trade-off to pay for. The collector's pause times do not grow with the heap, but its collection frequency does, so a small heap brings on early and frequent cycles. The JEP describes the older ergonomic behavior of committing one sixty-fourth of physical memory for the initial heap.
A team chasing fast startup set a tiny -Xms and accepted a long warmup, because the collector then had to acquire and prepare memory in increments while the application was already allocating. A team chasing fast warmup set a large -Xms, usually with -XX:+AlwaysPreTouch, and paid the whole bill before the first request landed. The JEP puts the spread at roughly a tenth of a second to start with a 2 MB heap against more than ten seconds with a 32 GB one on current hardware.
That work now happens in a new thread, ZMemoryWorker, one per heap partition. It commits and uncommits memory concurrently as capacity changes. It also heats memory before application threads reach it, which means pre-touching page…

articles.summary:
El doblez de una hoja de papel es una acción muy común. Sin embargo, si tratamos de hacerlo muchas veces seguidas, nos encontraremos con algunos problemas. Por ejemplo, cuantos más dobleces hacemos, menos superficie queda. También se va engrosando el paquete. Hasta aquí son problemas físicos. Pero, si dejamos de lado esto último, podemos seguir calculando. Es decir, podemos pensar en cómo sería el tamaño de una hoja de papel doblada muchas veces.
Con 27 pliegues por la mitad, tenemos un grosor teórico de unos 13,42 km. Esto quiere decir que el Everest está por debajo (su altura sobre el nivel del mar es de 8.848,86 metros). Además, bastaría con 15 pliegues más (42 en total) para tener un tamaño de unos 439.805 km, que es superior a la distancia media de la Tierra a la Luna. Estos cálculos están hechos en el caso ideal (sin limitaciones de una hoja real).
Simplemente vamos doblando por la mitad. Es decir, en cada paso multiplicamos el grosor por dos. Empezando con 0,1 mm, tenemos: 0,1 mm × 2 = 0,2 mm (primer doblez); 0,2 mm × 2 = 0,4 mm (segundo); 0,4 mm × 2 = 0,8 mm (tercer doblez)… En general, el grosor tras N dobleces es 0,1 mm × 2^N.

articles.title: AI Agents Are Creating a Shared Responsibility Gap
articles.summary:
Frontier AI labs are very clear about their responsibilities: making the model more robust, better guarded, and harder to hijack. They are also clear about what they can’t do, which is understand the business context of an action. An agent deleting files from Google Drive could be malicious or perfectly normal. They can't tell.
That raises questions about the shared responsibility model for Agentic AI. In cloud security, there is a clear separation of responsibilities between cloud vendors and their customers. If you copy data from AWS into SFDC, each vendor is responsible for the data's infrastructure security while they have it, but the customer is responsible for the action.
The AWS Shared Responsibility Model is a classic example.
The separation isn’t nearly as clean for AI agents. Agents act as intermediaries between you and the request, and that intermediary isn't deterministic by nature. It sends authenticated, authorized requests that can be compromised or rogue.
The first scenario is somewhat clear and goes back to what the AI labs try to prevent: a rogue agent has either misunderstood something or acted in a way it shouldn’t. A human mistake, only not human and not necessarily a mistake.
Five organizations have published guidance on responsibility for AI agents: shared responsibility models from Microsoft, CSA and CoSAI, AWS's security guidance for AgentCore, and Anthropic's “Trustworthy agents in practice.” Only two assign ownership of an agent’s identity, and they…

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Securing AI Agents in Production
articles.summary:
Securing AI agents is a variation of the insider-risk problem, requiring distinct identities, narrowly scoped credentials and fine-grained policy controls, according to Amanda Walker, senior director of engineering for privacy, safety and security at Google. In a QCon San Francisco session, she outlined patterns for teams whose agents have been adopted organically and are running ahead of their security and observability frameworks.
With agents now executing multi-step plans in live production environments, Walker argued that "a rogue AI agent is the same problem as a rogue human insider," one that acts with superhuman speed and persistence. Controls therefore need to work at machine speed, rather than relying on someone reviewing logs the next morning. She covered identity and credentials, boundary defence, subagent orchestration and policy-based containment.
Walker described giving an agent raw human credentials as the fastest path to production failure. The agent inherits the user's authority, so a prompt injection in a document can turn that access to an attacker's purposes. She recommended explicit principals for agents, the AI equivalent of service accounts, so each agent can be provisioned and logged separately without impersonating anyone.

articles.title: En 1724 cayó un meteorito en Alemania: acabamos de descubrir que contenía un material 'imposible' para la física
articles.summary:
El meteorito de Steinbach fue hallado en Alemania en 1724. Alguno de sus fragmentos está en el Museo Nacional de Historia Natural de París. De él han estudiado una peculiaridad de su conducta térmica. Concretamente, han medido la conductividad térmica de uno de sus minerales en función de la temperatura. Se trata de un mineral que presenta un comportamiento poco habitual. Este estudio nos ayuda a conocer mejor los materiales que presentan comportamientos híbridos entre cristales y vidrios.
El mineral en cuestión es la tridimita. Es un tipo de dióxido de silicio similar al cuarzo, aunque estructuralmente diferente. En la muestra del meteorito que han estudiado, observan que la conductividad térmica de este mineral es casi constante en el rango de temperatura de 80 a 380 kelvin (que se corresponden aproximadamente con -193 y 107 grados centígrados). Este estudio se publica en PNAS el 11 de julio de 2025.
Dos mecanismos que se compensan
En materiales cristalinos sencillos, suele observarse que la conductividad térmica disminuye con el aumento de temperatura. Esto es debido a que el mecanismo de transporte de calor es el de propagación de vibraciones de la red. articles.title: Why Photonic Design Is Becoming a System-Level Challenge
articles.summary:
A component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Photonic engineers make design decisions at many levels.
A laser has its own performance requirements. So does an optical fiber. The interface between them introduces another set of variables. Ultimately, those individual components have to perform together as part of a complete optical link.
If the individual pieces meet their design targets, will the complete system perform as expected?
Not necessarily.
A Keysight EDA-Photonics Design (VPIphotonics) study of short-reach datacenter links provides a useful example. Two multimode VCSEL channels were designed with comparable signal characteristics and evaluated with a wideband multimode fiber. Yet when evaluated as complete transmission links, the two channels produced different results.
Understanding the difference in performance requires looking beyond any single component.
The VPIphotonics study modeled 26.5625 GBaud PAM4 transmission over 150 meters of wideband multimode fiber, using VCSEL channels operating at 850 nm and 910 nm. Each VCSEL was modeled with four transverse modes, and the link considered coupling conditions and receiver models.
25 Gbaud PAM4 with a multimode VCSEL and OM4 fiber.
At first glance, the two channels seemed comparable.
The calculated 3 dB bandwidth was 27.0 GHz at 850 nm and 27.8 GHz at 910 nm.

“We are re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets — so our approach reflects current operating realities while keeping progress transparent year over year,” wrote Rachel Peterson, vice president of data centers at Meta, and Blair Swedeen, global head of net-zero and sustainability at Meta, in the introduction to the company’s 2026 sustainability report.
That’s a lot of words to say that Meta will continue to pollute if that means it can continue its AI rollout.
Such is the risk of voluntary targets. Companies can make and break them with little to lose, betting — often rightly — that they can ignore them with just a small hit to public opinion, which is fickle anyway. (Remember the Cambridge Analytica scandal? Most people don’t.) There’s almost no risk to the bottom line.
“We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline and interim milestone. We’ll continue investing in emissions reductions and reporting our progress annually,” a Meta spokesperson told TechCrunch.

articles.title: AI agents design new CPU architecture that's 4x more efficient than a conventional core, startup claims
articles.summary:
Forward-looking: Brand-new CPU architectures are rare, since even designing a regular CPU core can take a large team of engineers years. However, a Palo Alto startup called Architect Labs now says its AI agents came up with one largely on their own, right down to the final chip layout. The company also claims its Frostbite design is over four times as efficient as a conventional core.
Humans did pick what the chip should be good at, selecting 25 test programs, ten of which the agents could use to tune their designs. Beyond that, the AIs had no starting design to build on, according to a research post the company published last week, so they started out by combing through research papers and benchmarks, then prototyped candidate designs as simple Python models.
They eventually landed on interaction nets, an idea introduced in 1990 that treats a program as a web of connected nodes. The program then runs by rewriting pairs of those nodes over and over. Those rewrites never get in each other's way, so lots of them can happen at once. That means the chip doesn't need complex hardware to hunt for work it can run in parallel.
The agents' first spec ran to 141 pages, but the team ended up deleting it. Once the first circuit design came in, many of its numbers turned out to be physically impossible. After that, swarms of agents pitched changes in parallel and tested each one against a fast software model of the whole chip.

articles.title: Hope Is Not A Strategy: What First-Silicon Success Really Takes
articles.summary:
Most re-spins are caused by logic and functional flaws, not hard-to-predict physical effects.
Only about one chip in twenty now works the first time it comes back from the fab. For an industry that invests years and millions in every tape-out, that is a disconcerting thought.
It was also the starting point for a recent episode of ‘Wearing Flip Flops’, where host Ronen sat down with Axiomise CEO Ashish Darbari. The conversation traveled from AI silicon and power bugs to the place of formal engineers in a verification team. But one idea ran through all of it: Hope is not a strategy. Determinism is.
Here is what that idea means in practice and why we believe it matters more today than ever.
The latest Wilson Research Group functional verification study puts first-silicon success at around 5%, down from 14% in 2024. At Axiomise, that number doesn’t surprise us.
Look at who is building chips. Two years ago, the survey was shaped by a wave of new RISC-V teams, where design was moving faster than verification could follow. Today it is the turn of custom AI silicon, built not only for hyperscalers but for phones and cars too. For verification, this is an unknown territory.
Formal is in more projects than ever, perhaps 30 to 40% of them. But “using formal” can mean very different things. It might be a lint or connectivity app, assertions that only ever run in simulation, or formal trusted to sign off functional verification. Only the last really improves the chances of success at tape…

articles.title: Amazon snaps up Decart's AI optimization tech for $7.5B as it prepares to sell Trainium chips
articles.summary:
Amazon has agreed to acquire a good chunk of Israeli startup Decart.
The e-commerce and cloud giant is paying $7.5 billion for the startup, according to Bloomberg.
Decart has made a name for itself building interactive real-time world models — most recently Oasis 3 — and AI video-generation tools. But under the hood, the company stands out for its Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), software that helps AI models run efficiently on Nvidia, Amazon, and Google’s hardware.
As part of the deal, Amazon will acquire the technology behind DOS, as well as Decart’s founding team and team of AI researchers and engineers, Amazon said in a blog post.
“Every leap forward in AI starts with getting more out of every chip,” said Peter DeSantis, SVP of foundational AI models, custom silicon, quantum computing, at Amazon. “More efficient compute means better training, better reinforcement learning, faster inference, and better models for customers at a lower cost.”
Amazon, which has so far been using its Trainium chips at its own data centers, is preparing to start selling them to customers as a competitor to Nvidia. Decart’s technology could make it easier for customers to run their workloads on Amazon chips, rather than Nvidia’s, which has been the gold standard so far.
Decart and Amazon did not immediately return requests for comment.

Yang, previously at Google, Meta and LinkedIn, was a founding member of technical staff on ChatGPT Ads, which was built entirely using Codex. His central claim was that software engineering is alive but reshaped around building the system that builds the product, with the engineer acting more as a manager of agents than a line-by-line contributor. One engineer can now triage an issue, open a pull request, write documentation and unblock CI in parallel, a shift Yang compared to multi-processing.
Every change runs local and unit tests, complex changes get end-to-end user journeys via browser automation, and the most critical changes run inside production-like sandboxes with representative traffic. Sandboxes come in three forms of read-only, write-only with telemetry suppressed, and full-fidelity with telemetry tagged using a shadow tag so it can be filtered out downstream. Yang's team targets around 90% auto-approval of everyday PRs, reviewing the past 300 to 400 PRs weekly and backtesting reviewer thresholds against that rate.

articles.title: OPINION: Europe's rearmament risks creating empty factories
articles.summary:
Weapons factories are springing up all over Europe as proof, many say, that the continent is taking its rearmament seriously. It seems so simple. Build factories, manufacture arms and kit, and Europe, faced with aggression on its eastern flank and the changing realities of a complex, multipolar world, will be able to take care of itself and its interests after decades of low defence investment.
Of course, it is not so simple. Because supply chains, the networks of production and distribution on which all manufacturing relies, are not all in Europe, and do not scale in proportion to manufacturing.
To think that they do is to believe, wrongly, that a company may get funding, massively improve its production capacity, and never have to worry that a chip, or some unusual component, might stop it from manufacturing anything.
Factories do not exist in isolation: they rest on broad industrial foundations, the absence of which means they cannot deliver. Hence Europe cannot both rebuild its defence industry and let its wider industrial base atrophy. To ramp up military manufacturing is also to ramp up manufacturing as such.
The industrial policy question
The question, then, relates not to whether Europe has enough factories. Indeed, weapons factories are expanding at three times the rate they did in peacetime, covering some 7 million square metres of new industrial development, but whether Europe is pursuing the right industrial policy.

articles.title: “Si arranca y se mueve, no pasa nada”: la lógica que más llena los talleres, según un mecánico con 18 años de oficio

Por eso se puede asumir que es por los kilómetros. Posponer los mantenimientos tiene sus consecuencias, advierte Juande Rodríguez (mecánico con 18 años de experiencia).
“El error más caro es acostumbrarse a que el coche ya no va como antes”. Empezó en los talleres con 16 años. A los 20 abrió su propio negocio. En su currículum destacan ocho años de mecánica de competición. Deja claro que, aunque el coche siga siendo operativo, es importante actuar ante los primeros síntomas.
Por ejemplo, el color del humo que sale por el escape puede ser indicativo. Si tenemos pérdida de potencia y sale humo blanco o azulado, es posible que sea el turbo. También puede ir asociado a consumo de aceite. Es fundamental saber cuál es el origen.
El humo negro puede hacer referencia a problemas en la admisión. Por ejemplo, si el filtro de aire está tapado, no llega suficiente aire al motor. También puede haber pérdida de potencia sin humo. En este caso, la causa puede ser un sensor de admisión sucio o carbonilla.

- Date:

- Source:

- Summary:

Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
- Share:

When an app sends a request, OpenRouter forwards it to a provider that runs the selected model and passes the answer back.
Operational technology security company Dragos alerted OpenRouter after sending two million test prompts through the platform, each containing a unique tracking link or decoy credential, and detecting "activity indicating that data from at least three AI providers was exposed."
Dragos discovered that, in some cases, those credentials were leaked to outsiders and used in the wild, indicating that the test prompts had escaped.

Y, en unas declaraciones a Deadline que recoge el portal neozelandés Rova, lo ha resumido así: “Fue precioso y surrealista, y parecía que no hubiera pasado el tiempo”.
Un viaje atrás en el tiempo. Según cuenta el actor, volver al plató fue como regresar al pasado, y le bastó con mirar hacia abajo para que el cuerpo recordara lo que ya había vivido: “Ya he visto estos pies así, conozco este vestuario”. Vamos, que tiró de memoria muscular. Y es que, como explica él mismo, la sensación lo transportó de golpe: “Es como si de repente se esfumaran 27 años y estuvieras otra vez ahí dentro”.

Every diagnostic assistant, predictive model, or automated business tool comes with an infrastructure bill. Companies need computing power to train and run models, data to make those models useful in local markets, and specialised engineers to develop and maintain the technology.
Much of the infrastructure is priced in dollars, while these businesses largely operate in markets with significantly lower purchasing power.

Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.
The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.

articles.title: Que signifie la petite clé qui apparait en haut à droite de votre smartphone Android ?
articles.summary:
L’icône en forme de petite clé qui s’affiche dans la barre d’état de votre smartphone Android signale simplement que votre trafic web passe par un VPN. Android l’active dès qu’un réseau privé virtuel chiffre les données Wi-Fi ou mobiles de votre appareil.
À quoi sert un VPN sur Android ?
Installé sur un téléphone ou une tablette, un VPN (réseau privé virtuel) sert d’abord à créer une liaison chiffrée entre votre appareil et internet. En masquant votre adresse IP réelle (pour la remplacer par une autre), il empêche votre fournisseur d’accès ou l’administrateur d’un Wi-Fi public de voir vos activités en ligne. Vos données circulent à l’abri des regards indiscrets, ce qui est un bon moyen pour sécuriser votre navigation.
L’autre usage très répandu d’un VPN est le contournement des restrictions géographiques qui permet de simuler une connexion depuis un autre pays. Cela permet notamment d’accéder à des catalogues de streaming vidéo ou des contenus bloqués dans le pays où l’on se trouve. Pour autant, un VPN ne garantit pas totalement votre anonymat. En effet, si vous restez connecté à vos comptes Google ou Facebook par exemple, les sites peuvent toujours suivre votre profil utilisateur.

Ce pictogramme confirme donc qu’un VPN est activé sur votre appareil. Si la clé disparaît, cela signifie que le chiffrement ne fonctionne plus. C’est donc un moyen très utile de voir en un coup d’oeil que votre connexion est sécurisée. La plupart des …
