AI may not work like the human brain after all, scientists discover
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  York University
- Summary:
  AI may not think like the human brain after all, according to a striking new discovery that challenges how scientists understand artificial intelligence. Researchers found that even AI models that closely predict brain activity may rely on internal processes the brain doesn't use, raising important questions about their reliability in neuroscience research.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence may be much less like the human brain than scientists have long assumed. A new study from York University has uncovered a surprising weakness in AI models that are widely used to understand how the brain processes visual information.
For years, researchers have relied on artificial neural networks (ANNs), computer systems designed to perform tasks such as recognizing objects in images, to investigate how vision works. Over the past decade, these models have become some of the leading tools for explaining the brain's visual system. Their ability to reproduce patterns of brain activity has made them especially valuable in neuroscience.
But the new findings raise an important question: Just because AI can successfully imitate certain responses in the brain, does that mean it actually processes visual information in the same way?

articles.title: AI Vs. High-Level Synthesis
articles.summary:
AI promises to automate chip design from spec to implementation, but can it match HLS in productivity, verification, and quality of results?
Key Takeaways:
- The main advantage provided by HLS is productivity, but those gains diminish if not accompanied by a robust verification methodology.
- AI agents around current HLS tools will allow more exploration and build on existing trust but full AI potential may want to work outside those bounds.
- Producing RTL is the easy part. HLS has to generate RTL that is implementable, that meets power, performance and area constraints, within a defined context. AI struggles with this today.
High-level synthesis (HLS) initially struggled to find a market, but eventually it became a valuable tool for certain kinds of design. It is now threatened by the promise of AI, which some predict will allow engineers to go from specification to finished silicon while avoiding many EDA tools, including HLS.
Most developers of HLS solutions are not troubled by this today, though they do see many changes on the horizon.
HLS has been most valuable for algorithmic accelerators, although that could change. “When I have something that is too slow or power hungry to run on a CPU, I may want to look at custom silicon,” says Stuart Clubb, technical product management director at Siemens EDA. “I might choose to go the path of IP reuse, and that is the most likely answer for a bus interface or peripheral. articles.title: Why AI Struggles To Reuse Chip Designs
articles.summary:
AI can accelerate derivative designs, but physical constraints and incomplete data limit how much can be automated.
Key Takeaways:
- AI can accelerate derivative chip design, but those derivatives may not be physically viable or cost-effective.
- AI-assisted reuse depends on the availability of accurate design data, engineering knowledge, and proven methodologies.
- End-to-end automation is limited by gaps in multi-physics simulation, implementation, and verification.
Chipmakers are seeing mixed results when they apply AI to derivative and new chip designs, finding that AI-generated solutions can be substantially different and more costly than expected, and that AI-driven designs introduce new manufacturing and verification challenges.
Several key problems have emerged when incorporating AI in chip design. Among them:
- The data needed to ensure that follow-on designs will function as expected may not be complete because some of that data resides in other companies, such as foundries, OSATs, and various equipment and process providers;
- Integrating rapidly evolving AI capabilities into established EDA flows remains challenging, especially where predictability, traceability, and silicon-proven results are required.
- Many organizations have customized tools for their own chips, markets, and expertise, and AI tools have not yet adapted to those changes.

articles.title: F1 in Las Vegas: You’ve never seen an F1 race like this before
articles.summary:
Las Vegas welcomed Formula 1 to its streets this past weekend. And for the first time since the event’s inception in 2023, the Grand Prix delivered on a long-promised spectacle. The racing was closer to an IndyCar oval race than anything F1 fans will have seen since slipstreaming was the order of the day at places like Monza and Hockenheim, back when humans were still landing on the Moon and downforce had yet to fundamentally change racing.
The Vegas street circuit—the one that looks like an upside-down pig—is an extreme outlier on the calendar. It has plenty of long straights, so this year’s cars still suffer from energy starvation throughout the lap, as the inadequate size of their lithium-ion hybrid batteries means they become depleted very quickly, leaving the cars on just over half power with their V6 engines operating without the benefit of the hybrid’s electric motor.
And because it takes place at night, in the desert, in November, it’s cold—much, much colder than anywhere else the sport will visit all year. This coming weekend in the Middle East, track temperatures may well exceed 122° F (50° C ); on Saturday night in Nevada the track was a mere 59° F (15° C). Combined with the concrete streets, that spells low grip, but there is an added benefit—virtually no tire wear or overheating.
FP1 was completely rained out. A few drivers completed installation laps, but the risk of a crash was far too high.

Microsoft iniciou a distribuição automática do Windows 11 26H2 em PCs que já utilizam as versões 24H2 ou 25H2.
O seu computador já roda o Windows 11 26H2? Se não, saiba que, em breve, o sistema operacional será atualizado automaticamente para essa versão. A condição para isso é a de que o seu PC já tenha o Windows 11 24H2 ou 25H2.
A Microsoft liberou o Windows 11 26H2 oficialmente em setembro. Mas, até recentemente, a atualização para essa versão requeria que o próprio usuário acessasse o Windows Update para baixar e instalar o pacote. Um número restrito de computadores teve acesso à atualização automática desde então.
Em um anúncio recente, a companhia revelou que a atualização automática começará a ser liberada massivamente, ainda que de modo gradativo (alguns computadores terão acesso a ela antes do que outros). Isso significa que o pacote 26H2 será instalado em segundo plano, sem que o usuário tenha que executar alguma ação para isso.
Em linhas gerais, sim. O pacote 26H2 é considerado seguro por, entre outras razões, preservar a estrutura básica já existente nas versões 24H2 e 25H2 (todas essas versões compartilham os mesmos arquivos essenciais), bem como trazer recursos que já haviam sido liberados em atualizações anteriores, o que significa que, em muitos casos, o pacote de instalação não é grande.

The Borslon mouse, sharing a product and brand name, is a wired, “finger-worn gaming mouse,” as the brand describes it. It has all the spec numbers you’d expect from a good gaming mouse: a PAW3395 sensor, an 8,000 Hz polling rate, 0.125 ms response time, programmable buttons, and weighs 36g. However, the specs are often only the base level for performance; how it performs in the real world could be a very different story.
This product targets FPS gamers, and in the FPS gaming niche, there is an even smaller niche — aimers. These aiming communities focus purely on the mechanical skill of precisely landing shots on targets, experimenting with techniques and devices to improve their aim. Fünf Physiker der University of Queensland im australischen Brisbane haben erstmals eine digitale Botschaft allein über Schwankungen der Anziehungskraft gesendet. Sie übertrugen das englische Wort „Gravity“ durch eine 27 Zentimeter dicke Mauer, wie ihre Studie im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science Advances beschreibt.
University of Queensland nutzt alten Aufzug als Sender
Als Signalgeber diente ein Aufzug aus den 1950er-Jahren, dessen rund 1,8 Tonnen schweres Gegengewicht aus Gusseisen zwischen zwei Etagen fuhr. Im benachbarten Waschraum stand auf dem Boden ein sogenanntes Gravimeter, also ein empfindliches Messgerät für winzige Veränderungen der örtlichen Schwerkraft.
Während Metallkäfige, Erdreich oder dickes Mauerwerk Funkwellen, Licht und Schall abhalten, kann kein bekanntes Material die Anziehungskraft von Masse blockieren. „Ein Gravitationssignal lässt sich nicht einfach abschirmen, indem man gewöhnliches Material in seinen Weg stellt“, erklärt Mitautor Charles Woffinden in einer Hochschulmitteilung.
Mit kosmischen Gravitationswellen, die erst bei schweren Himmelskörpern wie Schwarzen Löchern messbar durch das All laufen, arbeitet das System jedoch nicht. Stattdessen zog das bewegte Gegengewicht im Schacht lediglich eine kleine Testmasse an einer Feder im Messgerät je nach Etage unterschiedlich stark an.

articles.title: Nvidia employees greet Jensen Huang like a hero as he returns to company's HQ
articles.summary:
Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia’s offices on Monday to an applauding crowd of hundreds of employees, according to several videos circulating online.
The embattled Nvidia founder had stepped down earlier this month amid a series of scandals — including an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, which has triggered multiple Congressional hearings over national security, and two affairs with Nvidia employees — but was reinstated as CEO after pushback from the tech community and an intervention by President Donald Trump.
After basking in chants of his name, Huang briefly addressed the crowd.
“Thank you all for the second chance,” he said. “I’m going to be a better CEO the second time around.”
Over 200,000 people, including around 10,000 current Nvidia employees, had signed an open letter advocating for Huang’s return. Other tech leaders also pushed for Huang’s reinstatement, including Elon Musk, who said last week at the DealBook Summit that letting Huang go is like “kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you’re on a winning streak.”
Amid this increased scrutiny, however, other reports have depicted a different side to Nvidia’s top exec — one where Jensen is not seen as a beloved leader, but as a brutal bully. Based on decades of court documents and over a dozen interviews with current and former Nvidia employees, The New York Times reported that Huang “used humiliation as a tool” and verbally belittled staff at times.

articles.title: COP31 ends in failure as countries split over fossil fuels, climate finance
articles.summary:
ANTALYA, Turkey—By the time the United Nations COP31 climate talks ended Sunday afternoon, the conference center resembled a going-out-of-business sale at a pawnshop for broken dreams.
As cleaning crews cleared away the debris left by more than 100,000 participants, Murat Kurum, president of the Conference of the Parties and Turkey’s minister of environment, urbanization, and climate change, tried to tie together disparate parts of a draft climate deal with a shiny ribbon of multilateralism.
Many countries were not buying it.
For the first time since 2009, the conference ended without consensus on a cover decision, the concluding statement that typically signals global solidarity on how to confront the worsening climate crisis. Countries did adopt several decisions, including a program to help workers and communities transition away from fossil fuels, and a plan to assess progress on climate adaptation.
The failure to agree on an overarching conference statement reflected deep divisions over whether the agreement should mention fossil fuels and carbon capture, as well as how much climate financing developed countries should provide to developing nations hit by costly climate disasters.
The European Union, as well as several Latin American countries and Pacific Island states, said they would not accept the proposed text from the conference leaders.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO, Board Director
articles.summary:
Tech giant Nvidia has announced that it has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, Chief Executive Officer, and board member.
According to Nvidia’s press release, the board of directors voted unanimously to reinstate Huang after what it described as “a series of discussions and meetings,” during which the company was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s ability to lead Nvidia.”
Nvidia also confirmed that it received input from “senior levels of the United States government” and used that input to determine that Huang’s reinstatement posed no national security risk.
“I am honoured to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Jensen Huang. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment. I want to thank the Nvidia board for its confidence and deliberation through this process.”
Huang also added that “I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can’t wait to get back to work.”
To add some context, Nvidia opened an independent investigation into Jensen Huang after it was revealed that a woman he was having an affair with was an alleged Chinese spy. Eventually, Huang resigned from his position at Nvidia, with current executive vice president and CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO.
Interestingly, Nvidia’s stock price is up over 30 per cent since the announcement that he is returning.
Source: Nvidia

articles.title: Un telescopio en Sudáfrica captó una señal láser procedente de más de 8.000 millones de años luz, y los astrónomos saben de dónde viene
articles.summary:
El radiotelescopio MeerKAT de Sudáfrica ha detectado una especie de láser natural que emite en ondas de radio desde una galaxia a más de 8.000 millones de años luz. El descubrimiento fue publicado en febrero de 2026 por el Instituto Interuniversitario de Astronomía Intensiva en Datos (IDIA), y los astrónomos ya saben de dónde procede la señal y por qué ha llegado con tanta fuerza.
Un láser que emite en radio. El origen está en el gas de hidroxilo de las galaxias, que puede producir una emisión máser muy intensa, parecida a la de un láser pero en longitudes de onda de radio. Y cuando esa emisión se vuelve excepcionalmente potente, los astrónomos hablan de un megamáser. Vamos, que es un láser cósmico, aunque invisible para nuestros ojos.
Son fenómenos poco frecuentes que funcionan como balizas cósmicas y revelan información importante sobre las galaxias del universo primitivo.
Una lupa en mitad del camino. “Este sistema es verdaderamente extraordinario”, asegura Thato Manamela, investigador posdoctoral de la Universidad de Pretoria con financiación del Observatorio Radioastronómico de Sudáfrica (SARAO) y autor principal del estudio sobre el descubrimiento.

Vous pensez que pour créer une vidéo, il faut impérativement maîtriser un logiciel de montage ou d'animation ? Plus maintenant avec Hyperframes. Les compositions sont écrites en HTML, CSS et JavaScript, puis transformées en vidéo. Ce projet open source est surtout prévu pour travailler avec des agents IA capables de générer et modifier ce code.
Plus besoin de passer par un format propriétaire ou de construire une interface complexe avant de commencer. Une page HTML, avec quelques attributs pour définir le déroulement des séquences, peut servir de composition, être prévisualisée dans un navigateur, puis convertie en vidéo. Le framework fonctionne notamment avec Node.js et FFmpeg, et peut être utilisé directement à partir d'une ligne de commande.
- Rendu vidéo MP4 déterministe
- Projets éditables après création par agent
- Éditeur visuel dans le navigateur
Une page Web devient une vidéo
Convertir une page Web en vidéo : une idée qui peut paraître surprenante. Et pourtant, HyperFrames utilise les technologies déjà employées pour créer des interfaces Web comme matériau de base pour les animations. HTML et CSS définissent les éléments visuels, tandis que JavaScript les anime. Le framework accepte notamment GSAP, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js ou encore les animations CSS et Web Animations API.

articles.title: Math's biggest open problem may have fallen to AI, but the proof is unreadable to humans
articles.summary:
What just happened? Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, has published a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, a 167-year-old conjecture about the distribution of prime numbers and one of mathematics' most famous unsolved problems. He developed the proof with the help of Anthropic's Claude AI model. The organizations responsible for maintaining the field's leading proof-checking software verified it within a day of its release. It is the second of the seven Millennium Prize Problems to be solved with AI in roughly three months.
Alpöge did not release the proof as a traditional research paper. Instead, he posted it on his personal website in a formal programming language that allows computers to check every logical step. Within a day, reviewers from the Lean Focused Research Organization and the Mathlib Initiative had checked 17 million lines of code.
"We have full confidence that Alpöge's proof of the Riemann Hypothesis is correct," the two groups said in a joint statement. "We congratulate him on this achievement."
The speed of the verification came down to the format. A paper tackling a problem this difficult would normally face months or even years of expert review. A formal proof, however, can be checked mechanically. The software doesn't need to understand the reasoning or be convinced by it. It only needs to confirm that each step follows logically from the previous one.

Mais pour acheter les processeurs NVIDIA dont elle a tant besoin, l’entreprise s’est récemment endettée de, tenez-vous bien, 40 milliards de dollars. Et Elon Musk compte surtout exploiter cette technologie dans l’espace qui, selon lui, deviendra l’endroit le moins cher pour faire tourner les modèles. Il risque cependant d’avoir des bâtons dans les roues, et pas forcément ceux que l’on croit.
Des puces qui ne peuvent pas aller dans l’espace
Ici, il n’est pas question de défi de refroidissement ou de maintenance, mais surtout de créance. Car sous la houlette de géants de la finance comme Apollo et Goldman Sachs, SpaceX loue ces puces et verse un loyer qui sert à rembourser ses prêteurs. Plus de 30 milliards ont déjà été vendus à de grands investisseurs, dont Pimco, BlackRock ou KKR.
Or, dans ce genre de montage, les puces servent aussi de garantie. Si l’emprunteur ne paie plus, les prêteurs peuvent récupérer le matériel et le revendre. Une sécurité qui rend le crédit moins cher, d’autant que les puces gardent de la valeur : certaines H100 de 2023 se revendent encore à environ la moitié de leur prix d’origine.

Western intelligence officials worry that Russia could launch a nuclear-armed satellite into orbit before the end of the year, suggesting the country’s development of a satellite-killing weapon of mass destruction is more advanced than previously thought, German media reported Monday.
The orbiting nuclear weapon would threaten thousands of satellites in low-Earth orbit, including military and commercial communications networks like Starshield and Starlink. A nuclear-armed satellite would also put at risk Western military surveillance satellites and human spaceflight platforms like the International Space Station. A nuclear detonation in orbit would be indiscriminate, also knocking out Russia’s own spacecraft and Chinese satellites.
US lawmakers briefed on government intelligence first disclosed Russia’s ambition to deploy a space-based nuclear weapon in early 2024. At the time, US officials said Russia had launched a test satellite in 2022 to test the effects of radiation on space hardware and pave the way for a future nuclear-armed craft, but that Russia had not yet sent a nuclear weapon into orbit.
Reporting from three German news outlets—public broadcasters NDR and WDR and the Munich-based newspaper Süddeutsche Zeitung—indicates Russia’s launch of a nuclear-armed satellite could be imminent. The report says Western intelligence agencies, including the German Armed Forces and Federal Intelligence Service, believe Russia is preparing to deploy the weapon in space this year. …

articles.title: Quantum computing: Why African banks and telcos must prepare
articles.summary:
Quantum computers could one day break the encryption protecting financial records and sensitive communications across Africa. Machines powerful enough to do that do not exist yet, but attackers need not wait: they could steal encrypted information today and store it until the technology catches up. Security specialists call this “harvest now, decrypt later.”
Quantum computing uses the unusual behaviour of tiny particles to tackle certain problems that would take ordinary computers far longer to solve. If the technology becomes powerful enough, it could break some of the encryption that keeps financial records, private messages and other sensitive information secure. For banks and telecommunications companies, the concern extends beyond when those systems might become vulnerable to whether information stolen now will still need to be confidential when they do.
That mismatch is central to a new report by the Future Investment Initiative (FII) Institute, a data-driven, non-profit foundation with an investment arm, produced in collaboration with Accenture, a global professional services and technology consulting company. It argues that emerging economies must begin preparing their digital infrastructure before the threat matures.
Customer records, financial information and sensitive communications may need to remain confidential for years. Replacing the cryptography protecting them can also take years, particularly across complex networks of legacy systems and outside suppliers. …

Casi un siglo después, dos asociaciones ecologistas plantearon en octubre de 2025 devolver este felino al Pirineo catalán con una prueba piloto que todavía está lejos de convertirse en realidad.
Quién lo propone y cómo. La idea parte de Amics del Parc Natural de l’Alt Pirineu y de ADLO Pirineo, que quieren soltar varios machos castrados en el Parque Natural del Alt Pirineu, el espacio protegido más grande de Cataluña. Los animales podrían llegar de Rumanía, cuya población de los Cárpatos se mantiene sin grandes cambios o crece poco a poco, según el balance de la Comisión Europea para 2017-2023. ¿Y por qué castrados? Pues porque, según sus impulsores, así no podrían reproducirse, y el experimento se quedaría en un ensayo controlado para ver qué efecto tiene su presencia en el ecosistema.
Un felino mucho mayor que el ibérico. El lince boreal (Lynx lynx), también llamado euroasiático, es el mayor felino de Europa. También es bastante más corpulento que el lince ibérico, al que WWF presenta como su pariente más pequeño. Puede medir entre 60 y 75 centímetros de altura y pesar hasta 30 kilos, según la ficha de la especie del Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica, y entre sus presas están los corzos y los rebecos y, en ocasiones, los ciervos.

The user pointed the agents to a confidential board review and an internal customer spreadsheet as sources for the numbers, though no one asked for either file to be shared. The agents also had access to an approved press kit that could have been used instead. Of the 100 test runs, confidential data ended up on the public blog in 87.

Confidential data was found to have leaked in 57 of the 60 runs involving the open-weight models, which were also the worst offenders when it came to sharing entire documents. En 1997, cuando los investigadores analizaron el interior del sarcófago de la central nuclear de Chernóbil, encontraron creciendo en las paredes de la Unidad 4 un auténtico ecosistema biológico. En total identificaron 37 especies de hongos pertenecientes a 19 géneros distintos, con especímenes como Cladosporium sphaerospermum y Penicillium hirsutum. Y lógicamente, ver vida en una zona donde no debería existir es algo llamativo a cualquier nivel.
El secreto. Para entender cómo podía prosperar la vida en ese reactor radioactivo, los investigadores tomaron muestras y vieron que un pigmento oscuro que le servía de escudo era la clave de todo esto. Y no era ni más ni menos que la melanina.
Ahora, casi tres décadas después, aquel hallazgo ha servido de inspiración para crear materiales capaces de neutralizar algunas de las sustancias más peligrosas creadas por el ser humano, desde pesticidas agrícolas hasta agentes nerviosos como el gas sarín que se puede usar en una guerra química.
El pigmento que sobrevive a la radiación. Los hongos hallados en Chernóbil producen un tipo específico de melanina llamada alomelanina. Pero a diferencia de la eumelanina humana, la alomelanina carece de nitrógeno y posee una estructura química intrínsecamente microporosa que le permite actuar como una esponja molecular.

articles.title: Surveillance pricing uses our personal data to make us pay more
articles.summary:
“It costs what it costs” is a mindset I’ve found useful when encountering a sizable, but highly necessary or desired, expense. The sentiment encourages me to accept the price because that’s the accepted value of the gadget, app, or service that I really need or want.
But with surveillance pricing, that comfort is no longer a given. I could end up paying more for my TV because of where I am or more for a software subscription because of my age.
Surveillance pricing leverages data collected from our web history, smart devices, and apps with the goal of getting us to pay more. That obfuscates the value of products, challenges smart shopping and budgets, and makes it harder for people to get products and services at a fair price.
Surveillance pricing versus dynamic pricing
Surveillance pricing, according to the nonprofit Electronic Privacy Information Center (EPIC), is an algorithmic pricing practice that charges individuals or groups of individuals different prices “for the same goods or services.”
“The goal of surveillance pricing is to infer the highest price that the customer is willing to pay, based on consumers’ personal data and other market data,” EPIC explains.
Instacart previously practiced surveillance pricing, also called personalized pricing. It was the most simple of questions. On Monday afternoon, during a NASA news conference about the International Space Station, Space News reporter Jeff Foust asked about an upcoming launch of a Russian spacecraft.
“It’s my understanding there’s another cargo mission going to the ISS this week, a Russian Progress,” Foust said. “Can you confirm that, and give the date and time that will launch?”
This Progress MS-36 cargo launch, mind you, is presently scheduled for fewer than 16 hours from now, at 10:13 UTC (05:13 am ET) on Tuesday. It is going to a space station co-operated by the US space agency. But no, NASA would not provide this basic information about the upcoming Progress launch.
“Regarding the Progress launch, I would ask you to please reach out to Roscosmos directly for any questions tied to that vehicle,” said the senior NASA official on the call, Gaurang Patel, operations integration manager for NASA’s Low Earth Orbit Program.
Effectively, this is a “Go f- yourself” response from NASA. Roscosmos typically does not reply to Western media outlets, and everyone knows this.
So why is a bog-standard Progress launch suddenly a state secret? It seems to be a recent policy change, because, historically, NASA has televised every one of these cargo flights from Russia’s main spaceport in Baikonur, Kazakhstan. But there is no information about the upcoming launch on NASA’s television schedule for upcoming “live” events.

Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorrência no âmbito digital.

Le principe est que l'IA éclaire, et l'humain décide. A LocalCircles study finds that 94% of India's 354 most-used online platforms continue to deploy dark patterns, with 37 of 45 sectors having no fully compliant platform.
As many as 94% of India's most-used online platforms continue to use deceptive design practices, commonly known as dark patterns, despite growing regulatory scrutiny, according to a new study by LocalCircles.
The study analysed 354 online platforms across 45 sectors and found that only 20 were free of dark patterns. Further, 37 sectors had no platform that fully complied with the dark pattern guidelines.
The findings come weeks before the amended Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2026, take effect on January 1, 2027. Under the new rules, e-commerce companies must conduct annual self-audits and prominently display certificates declaring their platforms free of dark patterns.
Dark patterns or Dark UX are user interface designs that trick users into taking unintended actions such as buying a subscription, making payments or sharing personal data.
The study also found gaps in the self-declaration process. Of the 31 companies that had submitted a 'dark pattern free' declaration to the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), platforms operated by 23 companies, or 74%, were still found to have dark patterns. Only eight companies were found to be compliant.

Queda apenas unos días para el inicio oficial del Black Friday, pero los anuncios de ofertas llevan semanas bombardeándonos el móvil, el buzón de correo y las redes sociales. Entre esos anuncios hay algunas tiendas que prometen grandes ofertas, pero nunca han vendido nada y, aun así, lucen el logo de cadenas que todos conocemos.
Detrás de esas webs fraudulentas hay toda una maquinaria con plantillas, direcciones desechables y, cada vez más, inteligencia artificial para pulir el engaño y hacer creer a los usuarios incautos que han encontrado el chollazo del siglo. Repasamos cómo crece la suplantación de marcas y qué señuelos conviene reconocer antes de pagar.
Black Friday y Navidad: un terreno abonado
Las estafas van donde está el dinero, y en las campañas de Black Friday y Navidad hay mucho dinero. En España, el INCIBE gestionó 45.445 incidentes de fraude online en 2025, un 19% más que en 2024. También colaboró en el cierre de 4.600 dominios, sobre todo de tiendas falsas.
Este incremento del fraude en compras online no se limita a España, sino que es mundial. Según datos del Informe Norton Holiday 2026, la compañía de ciberseguridad bloqueó 526.000 dominios de tiendas falsas en el último trimestre de 2025, casi el doble que los 260.000 dominios fraudulentos detectados en 2024. Entre las más bloqueadas de 14 países, el 64% seguía en la lista seis meses después de detectarse. Es decir, este tipo de ciberestafas se intensifican en las campañas comerciales más potentes, pero no d…

articles.title: Cómo cancelar la suscripción de Nintendo Switch Online sin perder el acceso hasta el último día pagado
articles.summary:
Para cancelar Nintendo Switch Online hay que desactivar la renovación automática, no borrar la cuenta ni cerrar el servicio. Según la página oficial de asistencia de Nintendo, el trámite se hace desde la consola o desde el sitio web de la cuenta Nintendo, y debe completarse al menos 48 horas antes del vencimiento.
La suscripción sigue activa hasta que termina el período ya pagad y Nintendo aclara que no entrega reembolsos ni créditos por el tiempo que quede, de modo que cancelar con anticipación no recorta el servicio contratado.
Este proceso solo puede hacerlo la cuenta Nintendo que compró la suscripción. Si el plan es familiar, el resto de los integrantes del grupo tampoco podrá usar el servicio cuando el plan termine.
Una advertencia importante a tener en cuenta, es que una vez que se desactiva la renovación automática no es posible volver a activarla. Quien quiera retomar el servicio después deberá comprar una nueva suscripción.
Cómo hacer el proceso desde la consola
En una Nintendo Switch 2, hay que abrir Nintendo eShop desde el menú HOME y elegir la cuenta que compró la suscripción. Luego se toca el ícono de usuario, en la esquina superior derecha, y se baja hasta la opción de cancelar la suscripción mediante la desactivación de la renovación automática.

articles.title: Free corrige un bug qui faisait redémarrer la Freebox Delta en plein téléchargement
articles.summary:
Free a déployé lundi une nouvelle mise à jour du Freebox Server, sixième version depuis le 5 novembre. En plus de correctifs de sécurité, elle corrige un problème de stabilité qui pouvait figer, puis faire redémarrer, la Freebox Delta.
C'est une énième mise à jour que l'opérateur Free a décidé de déployer ce lundi 23 novembre 2026. Comme toujours, il faut redémarrer la box pour l'installer.
Une Freebox Delta qui gelait, puis redémarrait

Sa box se figeait une à quatre minutes, son interface ne répondait plus, puis redémarrait entièrement, en coupant au passage son réseau câblé pendant une bonne vingtaine de secondes. articles.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
articles.summary:
Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence. Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution.
They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched.
In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough.
According to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerabili…

articles.title: Independent Web Browser/Engine "Ladybird" Goes Into Alpha Release
articles.summary:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Independent Web Browser/Engine "Ladybird" Goes Into Alpha Release
One of the few independent web browser/engine projects, called Ladybird, has entered its alpha release, moving towards the final release. After four years of independent development, Ladybird is finally in alpha, allowing users and testers to try it out and provide feedback before the final version arrives. Originally, Ladybird was spun out of SerenityOS development with its browser engine and HTML viewer, later becoming one of the rare independent projects. As most modern browsers focus on monetizing their user base by collecting data or offering cryptocurrency tokens, Ladybird aims to challenge that and stand out as one of the few designs not based on Chromium, Gecko, or WebKit.
Modern browsers like Chrome run on Chromium, Firefox uses Gecko, and other alternatives like Brave and Edge also use Chromium, leaving little room for independence. Monopolies are inherently problematic, and Ladybird seeks to offer users a choice with a lightweight, modern browser focused solely on browsing the web. Furthermore, one of the most important aspects of human-machine interactions is the web browser, which should remain under user control and not become a tool for data collection. Supporting open alternatives is always a good idea, ensuring your freedom to browse without becoming a product or a target for ads is more important now than ever. Currently, Ladybird builds only for macOS and Linux, but…

articles.title: “Scénario catastrophe absolu” : la Russie se préparerait à lancer Sputnik-S, un satellite doté d'une ogive nucléaire
articles.summary:
Charge nucléaire en orbite : la Russie serait sur le point d'envoyer Sputnik-S avant fin 2026 menacer les constellations de satellites
Selon des médias allemands, la Russie serait sur le point d'envoyer en orbite terrestre un satellite muni d'une charge nucléaire. Illégal et excessivement dangereux, ce projet viserait à constituer une menace contre les constellations de satellites de type Starlink.
La Russie serait en train de finaliser l'envoi d'ici quelques semaines – avant la fin de 2026 – d'un satellite, Sputnik-S, doté d'une ogive nucléaire. C'est en tout cas ce qu'affirment des médias allemands. L'information est suffisamment prise au sérieux pour faire réagir l'OTAN, et le monde des agences spatiales, notamment l'ESA, l'agence européenne.
	
C'est le cauchemar ultime. Le scénario catastrophe absolu.
Une ogive nucléaire en orbite pour neutraliser les constellations de type Starlink ?
Déjà en 2024, des responsables américains avaient alerté sur un tel risque visant à détruire, ou désactiver, les constellations satellitaires dont l'utilité s'est depuis avérée redoutable en situation de conflit armé.
Mais cela est-il légal ? Non, le traité de l'espace de 1967 proscrit tout placement d'arme de destruction massive dans l'espace, que ce soit sur un corps céleste comme la Lune, ou en orbite terrestre.

articles.title: Decathlon confirme une fuite qui touche des clients de son site
articles.summary:
Decathlon reconnaît qu'un pirate a copié, chez l'un de ses prestataires, les noms, les numéros de téléphone et les adresses de clients de son site. Les fichiers qu'il a mis en ligne contiennent aussi des livraisons prévues cette semaine, celle du Black Friday.
Le pirate, qui se fait appeler 4me1, a diffusé quatre fichiers de clients de Decathlon sur PwnForums, un forum de cybercriminels, dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi. Contactée par Ouest-France, l'enseigne a confirmé dans la soirée un accès malveillant à des données de clients de decathlon.fr, le 22 novembre, chez un prestataire externe. Comme l'indique French Breaches, d'après Decathlon, le pirate n'a récupéré ni données bancaires ni mots de passe. Mais avec ces fichiers, n'importe qui peut savoir où, quand et comment des dizaines de milliers de colis ont été livrés.
Le pirate a récupéré les instructions laissées aux livreurs de Decathlon
Le fichier principal compte 163 646 fiches, et une personne peut apparaître plusieurs fois. Cyberattaque.org s'est procuré l'archive et a dénombré 137 549 adresses e-mail et 135 586 numéros de téléphone différents. Le deuxième fichier liste plus de 250 000 commandes passées entre juillet 2021 et le 21 novembre, avec leur date de livraison et leur statut.

Jones fue una de las figuras más visibles durante la crisis que atravesó la empresa y participa en los comités de auditoría y de nominaciones y gobierno corporativo.
Otro de los integrantes con trayectoria en el ecosistema inversor es Tench Coxe, antiguo director gerente de Sutter Hill Ventures, una firma de capital de riesgo. Dentro de Nvidia forma parte de los comités de auditoría y remuneraciones, dos áreas vinculadas con la supervisión financiera y las decisiones sobre compensaciones de los principales ejecutivos.

articles.title: 3D printer that promises simultaneous printing from all four heads gets $500,000 in crowdfunding — four-printhead Co Print Quadro MSRP set at just $899, promises reduced waste and faster printing
articles.summary:
3D printer that promises simultaneous printing from all four heads gets $500,000 in crowdfunding — four-printhead Co Print Quadro MSRP set at just $899, promises reduced waste and faster printing
The Co Print Quadro is this year's second IQEX 3D printer Kickstarter campaign, and it's much more affordable with an SRP of $899.
The Co Print Quadro is an Independent Quad Extrusion (IQEX) bedslinger 3D printer, carrying four fully functional printheads on one gantry. The 3D printer accessory company’s first 3D printer aims to bring IQEX technology to the masses at a budget price, with an SRP of only $899. It has already raised over $500,000, crushing its goal of only $9,820.
Independent Quad Extrusion, or IQEX, is unlike tool-changer 3D printers. Instead of one print head swapping assemblies, it has four individual print heads. This allows for increased productivity by printing with all four heads at once, or reducing waste by not going through any purging steps.
The Co Print Quadro is a non-enclosed bedslinger, and its design is quite similar to the Bambu Lab A1, albeit much beefier. The four print heads line up on one gantry, with space for three extruders on either side so they can get out of the way while either of the extruders on the edges can print. It has a large build volume of 300mm3, while the unit itself takes up a massive 780 x 620 mm footprint (2.5 x 2 feet).

articles.title: Cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne : des données personnelles ont été volées, des hackers chinois sont suspectés
articles.summary:
La cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne s’est bien soldée par une fuite de données. Ce lundi 23 novembre, l’exécutif a reconnu que l’EU Academy, une plateforme en ligne qui propose des formations et des ateliers conçus par les institutions de l’Union, a subi une fuite de données personnelles. Cité par Reuters, Thomas Regnier, porte-parole de la Commission pour les questions numériques, indique que « la plateforme EU Academy a été affectée par la campagne de cyberattaques détectée contre la Commission », qui a abouti à une « fuite de données personnelles des utilisateurs ». Toutes les victimes ont été informées « aujourd’hui via le site de l’EU Academy ».
À lire aussi : Piratage de frigos de supermarchés – une opération secrète a évité une catastrophe au Royaume-Uni
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Parmi les données compromises, on trouve les noms et les adresses e-mail des utilisateurs. Sans surprise, Bruxelles met en garde toutes les personnes concernées contre d’éventuelles campagnes de phishing. En effet, des pirates pourraient se servir des informations subtilisées pour envoyer des e-mails piégés et crédibles. Dos au mur, la Commission a mis la plateforme hors ligne jusqu’à nouvel ordre.
« L’incident fait toujours l’objet d’une enquête. L’accès public à la plateforme a été désactivé », indique le site de l’EU Academy.

articles.title: CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in record-setting $43.9B cybersecurity deal
articles.summary:
CrowdStrike to buy Zscaler in record-setting $43.9B cybersecurity deal
CrowdStrike Holdings Inc. today announced plans to acquire Zscaler Inc., a fellow provider of cybersecurity software, for about $43.9 billion.
The all-stock deal values the latter company at $260.40 per share. That’s a 34% premium to Zscaler’s closing price on Friday, the day CrowdStrike’s takeover interest became public. The transaction would be the largest cybersecurity acquisition on record by a wide margin.
Investors weren’t entirely thrilled. CrowdStrike’s shares fell 9% today, an indication that might think it’s an awfully large pill to swallow. Zscaler’s stock, however, rose almost 18%.
The companies reported their quarterly results in conjunction with the acquisition announcement. Both topped expectations across the board. CrowdStrike posted adjusted net income of $354.9 million on $1.58 billion in revenue, while Zscaler reported a $208.4 million adjusted profit and sales of $949.3 million. The former company also boosted its full-year guidance.
CrowdStrike’s flagship Falcon platform uses lightweight programs called sensors to protect employee devices, cloud instances and other technology assets. Zscaler’s Zero Trust Exchange, in turn, protects the network connections that link together those assets. The platform is positioned as an alternative to virtual private network tools.

articles.title: Wacom Goes Private in $860 Million Buyout Agreement
articles.summary:
Monday, November 23rd 2026
Wacom Goes Private in $860 Million Buyout Agreement
Wacom, arguably the industry leader in pen display tech for digital artists, and the maker of the EMR tech inside Samsung's S Pens, has officially declared that it is pursuing a buyout agreement to the tune of $860 million that would see the company return to private ownership. Currently, the Japanese tech maker is listed in the Tokyo Stock Exchange, but this will no longer be the case after the buyout, which will see Korean conglomerate, MBK Partners acquire the company. Wacom will retain its current president, Nobutaka Ide, who is currently facilitating the deal between Wacom and MBK. 
It is theorized that the move to go private was inspired by the accelerating rise of Chinese pen tech makers, like Huion and XP Pen, whose offerings often come dangerously close to Wacom's quality at significantly lower prices. The current buyout offer put forth by MBK Partners is roughly 55% higher than Wacom's per-share closing price as of November 20. The buyout agreement also follows a financial rough patch, during which Wacom failed to turn a profit for three consecutive years until the tide changed during the last fiscal year. articles.title: Los científicos españoles proponen reinundar el mar de Aral para evitar la emisión de cientos de millones de toneladas de CO₂
articles.summary:
Durante décadas, el mar de Aral fue el símbolo definitivo de la hubris humana contra la naturaleza. Y no es para menos, puesto que hablamos de un mar interior situado entre Kazajistán y Uzbekistán que pasó de ser el cuarto lago más grande del planeta a un desierto salino salpicado de barcos oxidados tras el desvío soviético de los ríos Amu Daria y Sir Daria para regar los cultivos de algodón. Pero lo que los modelos climáticos no habían detectado hasta ahora es que aquella catástrofe hidrológica seguía bombeando cientos de millones de toneladas de dióxido de carbono a la atmósfera.
Un estudio español. La investigación publicada en Science y liderada por el CSIC ha dado la vuelta a las cuentas de carbono en Asia Central, puesto que leojos de actuar como un sumidero de gases de efecto invernadero, el antiguo fondo del Aral ha liberado 748 millones de toneladas de CO₂ desde 1960.
De esta manera tenemos un auténtico tesoro oculto en el fondo del mar de Aral, puesto que el estudio apunta a que volver a inundar estratégicamente parte de su cuenca evitaría la liberación de otros 165 teragramos de carbono, lo que equivale a unos 605 millones de toneladas de CO₂ aproximadamente. Una cifra que no es pequeña, puesto que es aproximadamente tres años completos de emisiones de toda España.

Una plaga con sorpresa. Bertocchini las introdujo en una bolsa de plástico y continuó trabajando. Cuando regresó, las orugas estaban por todas partes y la bolsa estaba completamente agujereada.
100 orugas y 40 minutos. Intrigada por el descubrimiento, Bertocchini se asoció con Paolo Bombelli y Christopher Howe, investigadores de la Universidad de Cambridge. Sur iPhone, Chrome et Firefox affichent toujours les sites avec le moteur de Safari, deux ans et demi après l'entrée en application du DMA.
Sur votre iPhone, Chrome et Firefox ont l'allure de leurs versions pour ordinateur, mais ils affichent les pages avec WebKit, le logiciel de Safari qui transforme le code d'un site en texte et en images à l'écran. Apple impose ce moteur de rendu à tous les navigateurs de l'App Store. Le Digital Markets Act (DMA), le règlement européen qui encadre les géants du numérique, interdit cette règle dans l'Union européenne depuis mars 2024. Mais aucun éditeur n'a remplacé WebKit dans l'application de ses utilisateurs européens, selon l'association Open Web Advocacy. Avec Mozilla, Vivaldi, Shopify ou France Digitale, elle a écrit à Ursula von der Leyen, la présidente de la Commission européenne, pour réclamer une procédure formelle contre la firme de Cupertino.
Apple oblige Firefox à repartir de zéro pour changer de moteur
Depuis iOS 17.4, un éditeur de navigateur a le droit d'utiliser un autre moteur que WebKit en Europe, à condition d'obtenir une autorisation d'Apple et de respecter ses exigences techniques et de sécurité, rappelle iPhoneAddict. Already on launch day, it was well reported that GTA VI had shattered entertainment industry records, but it seems as though that was just the start of a legendary opening weekend. While Chinese sales are still low, it's worth noting that Western games generally don't sell as well in China, due to an already well-established local gaming market, and there is no official distribution channel for mainland China, so all sales came from gray-market imports.

Monday, November 23rd 2026
Report: Samsung's 2027 DRAM Supply Is Effectively Sold Out
If the global memory crisis wasn't already bad enough, it looks like relief is still quite a few years away. An exclusive report from South Korea's Economy Tribune says that most of Samsung's memory production capacity for 2027 through 2029 is already spoken for. The outlet says customers are already eyeing long-term agreements (LTAs) that run to 2031, and most are asking Samsung for volume beyond what they have already locked in. Samsung confirmed during its Q3 earnings call on October 29 that it had signed LTAs with 10 major customers and was negotiating with 10 more. The company aims to cover 60% to 70% of its memory supply with such deals by 2030. The Economy Tribune report says that new deals could come with pre-payments, as well as both upper and lower price limits.
That's the memory production capacity, but the more worrying part for PC builders is conventional DRAM. Industry leaders like Dell and SK hynix have already given timelines till 2030 for the situation to improve, and there looks to be no relief coming from Samsung's side either. Sources cited in the report say 2027 wafer capacity for commodity DRAM is effectively sold out. Moreover, DRAM bit supply growth is reportedly expected to top out at around 20% to 25% a year. As far as demand goes, memory makers can only meet 60% to 70% of the current demand, and that gap is expected to widen in 2027. That's not good news for anyone…

Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
Unix software enthusiasts, rejoice! An experimental project called "XNU Linux" has successfully booted a complete macOS 27 desktop on an ARM64 Linux system. This breakthrough offers a new way to run Apple's operating system without relying on traditional virtualization methods. This is significant news for the community, as there is a large group of enthusiasts eager to create custom macOS desktops, also known as Hackintoshes. The project utilizes Apple's open-source XNU kernel, modified to function as a loadable module within Linux, enabling macOS and Linux processes to run on the same hardware.
Instead of translating macOS applications into a format Linux can execute, XNU Linux takes a different approach by integrating Apple's kernel into the Linux environment. It consists of two primary components: xnu.ko, which runs the hosted XNU kernel, and fki.ko, which provides an interface to Linux resources such as memory, networking, timers, and storage. This setup allows macOS processes to run natively on the host CPU without an intervening hypervisor. The setup has been tested on an NVIDIA DGX Spark running Ubuntu, as well as an Apple Silicon Mac running Linux in a virtual machine. The system successfully reached the macOS desktop, including Finder, Dock, WindowServer, and loginwindow, with Safari and Chrome also operational. articles.title: Today I learned that Apple's newest iPhone Pro models are cooled using water vapor
articles.summary:
Today I learned that Apple's newest iPhone Pro models are cooled using water vapor
There's a sealed drop of water inside your iPhone Pro
The new iPhone Pro has water inside it and Apple put it there on purpose. Since the iPhone 17 Pro launched in September 2025, Apple's Pro smartphone models have all launched with a vapor chamber. It's a sealed metal pocket holding a tiny amount of water that boils and condenses to pull heat away from the chip.
Apple doesn't usually talk plumbing at its launch events, but this time it did. "Deionized water is sealed inside the vapor chamber," the company said in its press release, adding that the chamber is laser-welded into the phone's aluminum frame. Apple claimed up to 40% better sustained performance than the iPhone 16 Pro.
This came with a material change, too. The 17 Pro ditched titanium for an aerospace-grade aluminum unibody, which Apple said delivered the best thermal performance of any iPhone yet.
How a drop of water cools a chip
Most phones have long relied on solid plates of copper or graphite to spread heat. Those work, but adding more surface area usually means a thicker phone, according to IEEE Spectrum.
A vapor chamber does the job differently. The water evaporates near the hot chip, carries that heat across the chamber as vapor, then condenses back into liquid once the heat escapes into the phone's aluminum body. Turning liquid into gas soaks up a lot of energy, which is why the same trick has cooled laptops for decades.

Pour que ce soit pratique, Outlook, Teams et OneDrive fonctionnent en PWA, et disposent donc de leurs propres fenêtres. Teams peut même envoyer des notifications Windows. - Abuse of business applications and service provider-operated workflows, as opposed to direct exploitation of payment-related APIs.

Cybersecurity researchers have urged users to discontinue using a legacy ASP.NET anti-CSRF library named Idunno.AntiCsrf ("Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll") following the discovery of a critical vulnerability that has been exploited in the wild.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-131914, carries a CVSS score of 9.3 out of 10.0. The issue affects versions 0.9.1.0 and 0.9.1 Beta, and relates to an insecure deserialization vulnerability in the Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule HTTP module.
Idunno.AntiCsrf is a third-party ASP.NET IHttpModule designed to provide double-submit cookie Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) protection for ASP.NET WebForms applications. The open-source project is currently defunct and has not been updated since December 2008.
At its core, the problem stems from the fact that the module deserializes untrusted CSRF form token data using an unkeyed .NET System.Web.UI.ObjectStateFormatter instance without cryptographic MAC or signature verification when handling incoming HTTP POST requests to ASP.NET WebForms (System.Web.UI.Page) endpoints.
This behavior, in turn, can allow a remote attacker to achieve arbitrary remote code execution (RCE). Google's Mandiant division has given the vulnerability a "High" exploitability assessment, adding that exploitation hinges only on a single HTTP POST request with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token.

articles.title: N-able Discloses Critical Mail Assure Vulnerability Found During Breach Investigation
articles.summary:
N-able yesterday disclosed a critical flaw it found while investigating the breach of its Mail Assure and SpamExperts Hosted Cloud, an email filtering service it runs for managed service providers.
The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-134624, is a server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw. It allowed a user with high-level API access to open connections to internal systems of the user's choosing on the platform's servers.
The company fixed the flaw and restored access to the dashboard and APIs late on Saturday, closing an outage that began last Monday. Email delivery and spam filtering kept working throughout, according to the company. It has not said whether the flaw was the attackers' way in.
The bug sat in a connection check that Mail Assure runs for LDAP synchronization when a relay is configured. Before the fixed build, nothing restricted that check's destination, so the server could be pointed at any internal host and port to see which ones answered.
"An authenticated API user can cause the server to connect to arbitrary internal hosts and ports, determine which are reachable, and send crafted data to internal services.," the vendor's security advisory says.
The advisory gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.3, and lists builds earlier than 20261121.1943 as affected, with that same build as the fix. It does not claim code execution.

The activity revolves around CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS score: 9.9), a critical ScreenConnect client flaw that allows a guest to transfer and execute a malicious payload on a connecting technician's host.
"On November 12, 2026, we observed one managed service provider's (MSP) technician's workstation exploited to run a guest-pushed batch file, which then reported to a Telegram bot, downloaded an installer from masterdarky[.]com, and started a rogue ScreenConnect client pointing at the attacker's own relay, all in about 9 seconds," Huntress security researcher John Hammond said.
The batch script, "update_224ac089.bat," is designed to decode a Base64 Telegram bot token and chat ID, and register the new infection. Subsequently, it downloads an MSI installer that masquerades as a Windows update ("WindowsUpdate.msi") to launch a ScreenConnect client, enabling the attacker to gain remote access to the technician's machine.
The activity, observed between October 20 and November 16, 2026, is said to have sprayed servers blindly, with Huntress observing at least 688,000 guest "run file" requests for files named update.bat or update_<8 hex>.bat hitting 42 ScreenConnect servers from 29 IP addresses. articles.title: Critical binary-parser Flaw Enables JavaScript Injection via Malicious Parser Definitions
articles.summary:
A critical security flaw has been disclosed in the popular binary-parser library that could allow an attacker who controls parser definitions to execute arbitrary code.
The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-134814 (CVSS score: 9.2 / 8.1), is a case of code injection impacting binary-parser versions prior to 2.3.1.
"Binary-parser before 2.3.1 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers controlling parser definitions to inject JavaScript through string-typed options passed unvalidated by Context.generateOption()," according to a description of the flaw in the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).
"Attackers can supply crafted length, lengthInBytes, key, tag, offset, or namely() alias values to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the Node.js process when the parser is compiled."
According to an advisory released by the project maintainer on November 11, 2026, the problem arose from the fact that some user-controlled string options were inserted directly into the generated JavaScript code without adequate validation.
The parser options include -
- length
- lengthInBytes
- key
- tag
- offset, and
- the alias passed to namely()
"Parsing untrusted binary data with a trusted parser definition is not affected," Keichi Takahashi, who maintains the library, said. "These options are now validated as identifier paths (e.g. foo, $parent.len). Expressions such as 'len - 1' are rejected; use a function instead."

articles.title: “La superintelligence arrive” : pourquoi l'avertissement du chef de l'IA de Meta agace au plus haut point
articles.summary:
Alexandr Wang, le patron de l’intelligence artificielle chez Meta, prévient que la superintelligence est en route et que l’humanité pourrait en perdre le contrôle. Un cri d’alarme qui ne passe pas.
Car depuis le mois de septembre, les alertes sur une IA qui pourrait échapper à tout contrôle se multiplient. Et visiblement, Alexandr Wang, recruté l’année dernière par Mark Zuckerberg pour diriger sa super équipe de chercheurs, est lui aussi inquiet. Dans un essai partagé sur X.com, anciennement Twitter, il tire la sonnette d’alarme.
« Un esprit extraterrestre que nous ne comprenons pas »
« La superintelligence arrive », écrit-il. Selon lui, une IA plus capable que les meilleurs humains dans tous les domaines n’a plus rien de lointain. Son argument : la preuve de l’hypothèse de Riemann, un problème de maths resté sans réponse depuis 1859.
Obtenue par le mathématicien Levent Alpöge avec l’aide de Claude, elle a été validée par les communautés Lean et Mathlib, qui vérifient ces démonstrations par ordinateur. Wang y voit une découverte réalisée « avec l'aide d’un esprit extraterrestre que nous ne comprenons pas ».
Car Wang estime que Riemann est le sommet de l’intelligence humaine. « De nombreux physiciens s’accorderaient à dire que la découverte de la bombe atomique est un simple exercice à côté de l’hypothèse de Riemann », affirme-t-il. « Les lacunes restantes ne sont plus l'intelligence ; ce sont le savoir-faire propre à chaque domaine, la plomberie et l’expérimentation », poursu…

articles.title: Anthropic lanzó Claude Ship, una IA que revisa, corrige y aprueba el código de los programadores

Anthropic lanzó en versión de prueba Claude Ship, un conjunto de herramientas de su IA Claude que revisa los cambios de código propuestos por un programador, corrige sus fallas y decide cuáles están listos para incorporarse, según las reglas que fije cada equipo.
Esos cambios se llaman pull requests: propuestas para sumar código nuevo a un proyecto, que normalmente otra persona revisa y aprueba antes de que se integren. Según Anthropic, el objetivo es que el código se publique “tan rápido como los equipos lo escriben”, ahora que muchos programadores trabajan con asistentes de IA.
Claude Ship reúne tres piezas. La primera, Code Review, analiza cada propuesta, publica sus hallazgos y ya estaba disponible para el público general. Las otras dos, PR Steward y Claude Approvals, están en beta, es decir, en fase de prueba.
Tres agentes para revisar, corregir y aprobar
PR Steward actúa cuando una propuesta falla las verificaciones automáticas, tiene conflictos con otras partes del código o recibe comentarios de revisión. Después de cada cambio, deja un comentario con lo que modificó y cómo deshacerlo. Anthropic precisa que está diseñado para no aprobar ni fusionar propuestas.
Los desarrolladores pueden escribir “@claude” con una instrucción para orientar su trabajo, o “@claude stop” para que se detenga.
La decisión final la toma Claude Approvals, que aplica una política de aprobación escrita por el equipo en un archivo del repositorio, el espacio donde se guarda el proyecto. Puede apr…

The modified variant "implements various tricks to hide itself from security tools," Rapid7 said in an analysis, attributing it to the adversarial collective with moderate confidence.
First publicly detailed by Broadcom-owned Symantec in September 2022, Webworm is the name assigned to a China-aligned nation-state group that has targeted government entities, IT services, and electric power companies across Russia, Georgia, Mongolia, and several other Asian nations.
One of the tools used by the threat actor is a legitimate software called SoftEther VPN, with the bridge acting as a pathway connecting the compromised network and the attacker-controlled infrastructure.
The latest findings from Rapid7 revolve around a Windows executable ("netcapa.exe"), which is a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge ("vpnbridge_x64.exe") version 4.44, build 9807. The mutated version, rebranded as NtMonitor VPN, masquerades itself as Network Monitor Software from a company called Network Systems Solutions Inc. The artifact was uploaded to VirusTotal around mid-January 2026.

Para mantenerse en el aire de noche, estos vehículos dependen de baterías cuyo peso puede volverse, literalmente, su propio límite.
Un equipo de investigadores de la Universidad de Harvard y la Universidad de Míchigan, junto con socios de la industria aeroespacial, estableció la barrera técnica que hay que romper para que esos vuelos dejen de ser una promesa y se conviertan en una herramienta real de observación planetaria.
La clave está en un número: 500 vatios-hora por kilogramo. Esa es la densidad energética, dicho de otro modo, la cantidad de energía que una batería puede almacenar en relación con su propio peso, que los investigadores identificaron como el umbral a partir del cual el vuelo solar persistente se vuelve viable en gran parte del mundo.
Para ponerlo en perspectiva, las baterías de los autos eléctricos que circulan hoy rondan los 250 vatios-hora por kilogramo, la mitad de lo necesario. Celdas experimentales o de uso especializado disponibles en el mercado ya se ubican en torno a los 400, aunque a un costo todavía elevado.

Las cámaras de eventos llevan décadas prometiendo cambiar la manera en que los robots perciben el mundo. A diferencia de las convencionales, que capturan imágenes completas a intervalos fijos, estas detectan de forma continua cualquier cambio en la intensidad de la luz, de un modo que se asemeja al funcionamiento de la retina biológica. Sin embargo, había un problema que frenaba su adopción masiva: interpretar los datos que producen era una tarea enormemente compleja, y no existía una solución universal.
Cada segundo, una cámara de eventos genera decenas de millones de señales que no se parecen en nada a una imagen reconocible, sino a un torrente caótico de puntos luminosos. Para procesar esa información, los ingenieros debían diseñar algoritmos específicos para cada tarea y cada robot, lo que hacía el proceso lento, costoso y prácticamente imposible de escalar.
Un equipo de ingenieros de la Universidad de Pensilvania desarrolló una herramienta computacional de propósito general que, por primera vez, convierte esa avalancha de señales en información que distintos tipos de robots pueden utilizar directamente. El trabajo, publicado en la revista Science Robotics, se llama Fast Feature Field, abreviado como F³, y sus autores lo consideran un punto de inflexión en la historia de las cámaras de eventos.

articles.summary:
OpenAI and Cisco have teamed up to launch Shirudo (meaning "shield" in Japanese), an open-source Linux runtime that allows artificial intelligence (AI) agents to defend systems without downtime.
"It lets agents write dynamic eBPF controls to shield systems from exploits, giving defenders more time to test and roll out patches," OpenAI said in a post on X.
The AI upstart called the initiative a "first step" toward "self-defending infrastructure" that can adapt itself to new threats while the services continue to run and enable defenders to test and deploy fixes without any disruption.
The development comes as AI is accelerating vulnerability discovery, finding critical bugs in foundational software used to power internet-connected software.
Shirudo is being pitched as a way for defenders to test temporary safeguards (aka shields) and check if they block behavior that exposes a vulnerability, while letting legitimate requests pass through. Once a shield is approved by an operator, it can be deployed without having to stop the service.
The idea is to avoid a complete service disruption to block a line of attack simply because both an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same underlying Linux operation.
To achieve this, Shirudo makes use of eBPF (short for extended Berkeley Packet Filter), a technology that makes it possible to run lightweight, sandboxed programs inside the kernel without the need for modifying the system code or restarting it.

articles.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login
articles.summary:
A flaw in WHMCS's shopping cart, the billing and automation platform many web hosting companies use to run their businesses, could allow anyone on the internet to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from an installation's database. No login is needed.
The company disclosed the SQL injection yesterday along with two other flaws that need a logged-in client, and released fixed versions. It has not reported attacks using any of the three.
Because no login is needed, the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS score: 8.7), is within reach of anyone who can load the shopping cart of a vulnerable installation over the internet.
The records an attacker could pull include clients' personal and support information as well as admin accounts with their hashed passwords, according to the company's advisory. A stolen hash is not a working password, but it gives attackers something to try to crack offline.
The 9.0.10 and 8.13.8 updates shipped yesterday, and the release notes list them as maintenance releases. For the 9.1 series, the security advisory names 9.1.2 as the fix, but that build had not yet appeared on the company's 9.1 release notes page at publication time.
Fixes are available only for supported versions, so installations on the 8.0 to 8.12 series must upgrade to a fixed release.
Installing the updates falls to self-hosted administrators, since WHMCS Cloud installations are updated automatically, according to the company's updating documentation.

articles.title: Desarrollan un nuevo método que podría producir hidrógeno verde con luz solar
articles.summary:
Producir hidrógeno con luz solar requiere un electrodo especial que capte esa energía y la convierta en una reacción química capaz de separar el agua en sus componentes. Durante décadas, el material de referencia para ese trabajo fue el dióxido de titanio, una sustancia estable, pero con una limitación importante: solo absorbe luz ultravioleta, la porción menos abundante del espectro solar.
Para aprovechar también la luz visible, los investigadores aprendieron a combinarla con nanocristales de sulfuro de bismuto y plata, que captan un rango mucho más amplio del espectro. La técnica establecida para adherir esos nanocristales al electrodo mediante deposición electroforética requería, sin embargo, una contradicción de fondo: voltajes superiores a los 200 voltios y disolventes orgánicos tóxicos, lo que contradecía de raíz la promesa de un proceso verdaderamente limpio.
Esa contradicción acaba de resolverse. Un equipo conjunto del Instituto de Ciencia y Tecnología de Daegu Gyeongbuk (DGIST, Corea del Sur) y de la Universidad Kookmin logró depositar esos nanocristales sobre un electrodo de dióxido de titanio en agua y a apenas 4 voltios, el equivalente a una batería doméstica.
El resultado es un fotoelectrodo que multiplica por diez la corriente generada bajo luz solar respecto a los electrodos convencionales de un solo material, sin emplear plomo, cadmio ni disolventes peligrosos. Surfshark ajoute à ses forfaits One et One+ un filtre qui repère les appels frauduleux sur Android et iOS. L’application compare chaque numéro inconnu à une base de numéros signalés, puis prévient l’utilisateur ou, sur Android, peut bloquer l’appel.
Nous rapportions en août que Surfshark filtrait déjà les SMS frauduleux sur iOS et Android, avec un tri dans le dossier Indésirables sur iPhone et une alerte sur Android. L’éditeur s’attaque maintenant aux appels et publie une étude sur les numéros inconnus.
Un filtre usr iOS, un vrai blocage sur Android
Quand un numéro inconnu vous appelle, l’application le compare à une base de numéros déjà signalés. Surfshark assure qu’elle n’enregistre pas les conversations, ne surveille pas les appels privés et n’utilise pas vos données personnelles pour entraîner des modèles d’IA. Sur Android, elle repère les fraudes et le démarchage. En fonction du réglage, l'utilisateur reçoit un avertissement, ou l’appel est bloqué avant même que le téléphone sonne. Sur iPhone, une notification s’affiche sur l’écran d’appel avec l’une des sept catégories (fraude, démarchage, santé, services publics, administrations, collecte de fonds, services financiers). L'utilisateur peut décider de répondre ou non. En revanche, il n’y a pas de blocage automatique sur iOS.
L’étude porte sur 50 numéros inconnus en tête des recherches dans 32 pays. Ensemble, ils ont généré 13,2 millions de requêtes. Sept numéros sur dix sont liés à des fraudes et concentrent 72 % des req…

articles.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in bumper $44 billion deal set to shake up the security industry
articles.summary:
CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in bumper $44 billion deal set to shake up the security industry
CrowdStrike seals multi-billion dollar acquisition deal
- CrowdStrike snaps up Zscaler to help secure environments against emerging AI-related threats
- The company could get access to an additional 8,000 of Zscaler's customers
- Shareholders are worried about the massive deal, but Zscaler holders are happier
CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire cloud enterprise security provider Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth around $43.9 billion, as the company looks to position itself as an increasingly unified cybersecurity provider with its own endpoint and identity tools and Zscaler's network security.
Under the deal, CrowdStrike CEO George Kurtz will remain the CEO of the broader business, while Zscaler's founder and CEO Jay Chaudhry will still lead the Zscaler sub-business and join CrowdStrike's board.
However, CrowdStrike shareholders seem shocked and uncertain about the decision likely over concerns over share dilution and the broader risks of such a massive multibillion-dollar deal, with company shares falling around 9% on the day of the announcement.
CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler in a massive $44bn deal
Zscaler shareholders were more pleased with the news, with company shares rising 17% on the same day. Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares (currently worth a total of $237.18) for every one Zscaler share (worth $229.24 today).

articles.title: Plus besoin de retourner votre carte bancaire : Google Wallet va bientôt remplir votre CVV à votre place
articles.summary:
Google Wallet va bientôt remplir tout seul le code de sécurité de votre carte bancaire.
Wallet, le portefeuille numérique de Google, s’enrichit régulièrement de nouvelles fonctionnalités : suivi des dépenses avec l’assistant IA Gemini, paiement sans contact plus sûr, déverrouillage des serrures connectées et bien plus encore. Une autre nouveauté devrait aussi vous permettre de régler vos achats en ligne bien plus rapidement. On vous explique.
Google Wallet va pouvoir remplir seul votre cryptogramme
Jusqu’à récemment, quand on voulait payer un achat sur le web, il fallait aller chercher sa carte bancaire, la retourner et fournir les 3 ou 4 chiffres figurant à l’arrière. Ceux qui ont une bonne mémoire pouvaient aussi retenir le cryptogramme. Mais tout cela devrait bientôt changer : une nouvelle fonctionnalité est listée dans les notes de version v.2646 des services Google Play, qui ont été publiées hier.
Google Wallet se prépare en effet à inscrire votre CVV ou CVC à votre place lors de vos prochains paiements. À une seule condition : il faudra déverrouiller votre smartphone et vous identifier avec un code, un schéma ou une empreinte digitale. On ne va certainement pas se plaindre de cette couche de sécurité supplémentaire.
Une fonctionnalité qui soulève quelques inquiétudes

articles.title: Would you use earbuds that don't actaully play music? Nothing thinks you will, with its new Ear (note)
articles.summary:
Nothing's new AI earbuds have been officially teased, but don't expect them to play music
Pen and paper for the ears, anyone?
- Nothing teases Ear (note), new earbuds
- They're earbuds that record and transcribe your conversations
- Full release scheduled for December 8
Nothing has begun making some possibly concerning dalliances with AI tech, including its Nothing Ear (3a), which can record and transcribe calls or take 'Audio Snapshots' from voice notes you've been sent, or the Nothing Ear (3), with a Super Mic built into the case.
But until now, said buds have always played actual music too. Now, it sounds as if the company is ditching that aspect of its earbuds.
Nothing has begun teasing the new Ear (note), sharing some details with Bloomberg ahead of a full announcement on December 8. This looks set to be a transcription device, and many of these AI-toting gadgets have been coming to market over the last few years.
According to Bloomberg, both the earbuds and the case will have microphones embedded, and you can use them to record things around you. A companion app will let you access the recordings and their transcripts, all provided courtesy of AI.
A light indicator will show people that you're recording, though that's quite a half-baked measure to address the security concerns people have around this kind of spyware tech (not proving especially popular with those glasses, is it?), although Nothing has promised more ways it'll address security concerns. articles.title: Black Friday : 30 offres FOLLES chez Amazon, jusqu'à -67 % à 4 jours du 27 novembre
articles.summary:
À J-3 du Black Friday, les grandes marques de la tech se retrouvent en promotion chez Amazon, smartphones et Mac en tête. Nous avons retenu 36 offres en comparant chaque prix au prix barré affiché, et en vérifiant que le produit est bien vendu et expédié par Amazon.
Cette sélection s’ouvre sur les douze produits que nous avons testés, de l’iPhone Air à l’iPad Air M4, avant de passer à ceux que nous n’avons pas eus entre les mains. Elle couvre les smartphones, l’audio, le Mac, les TV et écrans de jeu, la maison connectée et l’électroménager, avec des remises de 9 % à 67 % sur le prix barré. La plus forte économie en euros concerne l’écran LG UltraGear de 45 pouces (800 € de moins), la plus forte en pourcentage la caméra Blink Outdoor 4 (-67 %).
